analysis.application_type: Liquid Staking Pool (Solana native "stake pool" program)
analysis.description: The SPL Stake Pool program pools users' SOL and delegated stake accounts across a set of validators, issuing a fungible "pool token" (via the SPL Token/Token-2022 program) representing a proportional claim on the pool's total stake. A "staker" authority manages validator membership and stake rebalancing between the reserve and validators, while a "manager" authority controls fees, configuration, and token metadata; end users deposit SOL or stake accounts to mint pool tokens and later withdraw stake accounts or SOL by burning pool tokens.

components.name: Manager
components.description: Keypair authority controlling pool configuration: fees, manager identity/fee account, optional funding (deposit/withdraw) authorities, and pool-token metadata.
assumptions: Assumed to be a semi-trusted administrative key.
Cannot mint pool tokens or move stake directly; fee increases and epoch/withdrawal fee changes are rate-limited and staged by the program.
Must control a valid SPL token account (matching the pool mint) to receive fees.

components.name: Staker
components.description: Keypair authority controlling which validators are part of the pool and how stake is rebalanced between the reserve and validators.
assumptions: Assumed to act to optimize pool stake distribution.
Cannot access user funds, mint pool tokens, or change fees/manager settings.

components.name: StakeDepositAuthority
components.description: Optional signer configured on the pool that must co-sign stake deposits when the pool is private; defaults to a program-derived address making deposits permissionless.
assumptions: Only relevant if the manager has configured a non-default (custom) authority via SetFundingAuthority.

components.name: SolDepositAuthority
components.description: Optional signer configured on the pool that must co-sign SOL deposits when the pool is private.
assumptions: Only relevant if configured by the manager; absence makes SOL deposits permissionless.

components.name: SolWithdrawAuthority
components.description: Optional signer configured on the pool that must co-sign SOL withdrawals when the pool is private.
assumptions: Only relevant if configured by the manager; absence makes SOL withdrawals permissionless.

components.name: UserTransferStakeAuthority
components.description: End-user (or delegate) signer that authorizes burning the user's own pool tokens on withdrawal and is set as the authority on the newly split stake account.
assumptions: Represents ordinary end users interacting with the pool; not a privileged system role.

components.name: SPL Token / Token-2022 Program
components.description: The standard SPL token program (Token or Token-2022) used for the pool's fungible token: mint_to, burn, and transfer_checked instructions are invoked by the pool via CPI.
assumptions: Trusted to correctly enforce mint/account invariants and only allow authorized mint/burn/transfer operations.

components.name: System Program
components.description: Standard Solana System program used to allocate and assign new stake accounts (validator/transient/ephemeral) and to transfer lamports (e.g. SOL deposits).

components.name: Native Stake Program
components.description: Solana's built-in stake program; the pool CPIs into it to split, merge, delegate, deactivate, authorize, and withdraw stake accounts (validator, transient, ephemeral, and reserve accounts).
assumptions: Trusted standard runtime program whose accounting (activation/deactivation epochs, credits observed) the pool relies on for correctness.

components.name: Metaplex Token Metadata Program
components.description: Third-party program used to create and update the pool token's on-chain metadata (name/symbol/uri) at a PDA derived from the pool mint.
assumptions: External program; the pool only issues signed CPIs to it and trusts it to manage the metadata account correctly.

components.name: Stake Pool
components.description: The single on-chain program implementing the liquid-staking stake pool: it owns the pool configuration and validator-list state, drives all stake account lifecycle transitions (creation, delegation, rebalancing, deactivation, removal), mints/burns the pool token on deposits/withdrawals, and manages the pool token's Metaplex metadata.

instructions.name: initialize
instructions.description: Creates a new stake pool: validates and stores the manager, staker, validator list, reserve stake, and pool mint, mints initial pool tokens matching any pre-funded reserve balance, and records the fee schedule.

accounts.name: stake_pool
constraints: must be owned by this program

accounts.name: withdraw_authority
constraints: address must equal the derived withdraw-authority PDA

accounts.name: reserve_stake
constraints: must be Initialized with zero lockup
staker and withdrawer authorities must equal withdraw_authority

accounts.name: token_program
constraints: must be a valid SPL token program id

accounts.name: deposit_authority
constraints: if present becomes both stake_deposit_authority and sol_deposit_authority

cpis.description: mint_to manager_fee_account for any pre-funded reserve lamports, signed by the withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: Manager must sign.
stake_pool and validator_list must not be the same account.
stake_pool and validator_list must be uninitialized, program-owned, and rent-exempt.
validator_list account size must exactly match the requested max_validators.
Fees and referral_fee must not exceed 100%/1.
Pool mint must have zero supply, 9 decimals, mint authority set to the withdraw-authority PDA, no freeze authority, and only supported extensions.
manager_fee_account must be a valid token account for pool_mint.
Reserve stake account must be Initialized, have no lockup, and have staker/withdrawer set to the withdraw-authority PDA.

If a deposit authority account is provided (and signs), it becomes both the stake deposit authority and the SOL deposit authority; otherwise a program-derived deposit authority is used and deposits are permissionless.

instructions.name: add_validator_to_pool
instructions.description: Adds a new validator to the pool by creating and funding a validator stake account from the reserve and delegating it to the chosen validator vote account.

accounts.name: stake_pool
constraints: last_update_epoch must not be behind current epoch

accounts.name: reserve_stake
constraints: must retain rent-exempt minimum after funding new stake account

accounts.name: validator_list
constraints: must not already contain the vote account

accounts.name: stake
constraints: address must equal PDA derived from [vote, stake_pool, seed]

accounts.name: system_program
constraints: must be the System Program id

accounts.name: stake_program
constraints: must be the native Stake Program id

cpis.description: allocate/assign to create the new validator stake PDA account, signed by the validator stake PDA's own seeds
split lamports from the reserve into the new stake account, then delegate_stake to the validator vote account, both signed by the withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: Staker must sign and match stake_pool.staker.
stake_pool must be valid and its last_update_epoch must not be behind the current epoch.
validator_list must not already be full and must not already contain the given vote account.
The stake account address must equal the PDA derived from [vote, stake_pool, seed].
The reserve must retain at least its rent-exempt minimum after funding the new stake account with rent-exemption plus minimum delegation.
A new ValidatorStakeInfo entry (status Active) is appended to validator_list.

instructions.name: remove_validator_from_pool
instructions.description: Marks a validator for removal by deactivating its validator (and transient, if any) stake account(s); the stake later merges into the reserve via update_validator_list_balance.

accounts.name: stake_pool
constraints: last_update_epoch must not be behind current epoch

accounts.name: stake_account
constraints: must be the correctly derived validator-stake PDA for the vote account in its delegation

accounts.name: transient_stake_account
constraints: if transient stake lamports recorded > 0, address must match derived transient PDA

accounts.name: stake_program
constraints: must be native Stake Program id

cpis.description: deactivate_stake on the validator stake account and/or transient stake account, signed by the withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: Staker must sign and match stake_pool.staker; pool must be up to date for the current epoch.
The vote account (read from the stake account's delegation) must be found in validator_list with status Active.
The stake_account address must be the correctly derived validator-stake PDA for that vote account.
If transient stake lamports are present, the transient stake account address must match the derived PDA and be deactivated if not already.
Status is updated to DeactivatingValidator/DeactivatingAll depending on transient stake state; preferred deposit/withdraw validator fields referencing this vote account are cleared.

instructions.name: decrease_validator_stake
instructions.description: (Deprecated) Splits lamports from a validator's stake account into a new transient stake account and deactivates it, moving stake toward the reserve on a later update. Fails if a transient stake account already exists for the validator.

accounts.name: validator_stake
constraints: derived validator-stake PDA must match; must retain required minimum after split

accounts.name: transient_stake
constraints: must not already exist; derived transient PDA

cpis.description: allocate/assign new transient stake account
split from validator stake into transient account; deactivate transient account, signed by withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: Deprecated; superseded by decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve. Fails if transient stake already exists for the validator.
lamports must be at least the minimum delegation; the validator stake account must retain at least the required minimum after the split.

instructions.name: decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve
instructions.description: Splits lamports from a validator's stake account into its transient stake account (creating it if needed, funding rent-exemption from the reserve) and deactivates it, so it can later be merged back into the reserve.

accounts.name: validator_stake
constraints: derived PDA check; must retain required minimum

accounts.name: transient_stake
constraints: must not already exist unless same seed reused

cpis.description: create transient stake account if needed
withdraw rent-exempt top-up from reserve into transient account (if needed); split from validator stake into transient; deactivate transient, signed by withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: Staker must sign; pool must be up to date; transient stake account must not already exist unless the same seed is reused (otherwise use the Additional variant).
lamports must be at least minimum delegation and leave the validator stake account at or above its required minimum.
Reserve must not be depleted below rent-exemption when funding the transient account.

instructions.name: decrease_additional_validator_stake
instructions.description: Decreases active stake on a validator again within the same epoch (even if a transient stake account already exists) by routing the split through a fresh ephemeral stake account before merging into the existing transient stake account.

accounts.name: validator_stake
constraints: derived PDA check; must retain required minimum

accounts.name: transient_stake
constraints: if already exists, seed must match recorded seed

cpis.description: create ephemeral stake account

withdraw rent-exempt reserve into ephemeral account (if needed); split from validator stake into ephemeral; deactivate ephemeral; merge ephemeral into transient stake account (or create+split transient directly if none exists), all signed by withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: Staker must sign; pool must be up to date.
If transient stake seed already in use, the provided seed must match it.
lamports must be at least minimum delegation and validator stake must retain the required minimum after the split.
Ephemeral/transient PDA addresses must match their canonical derivations.

instructions.name: increase_validator_stake
instructions.description: Splits lamports from the reserve into a new transient stake account and delegates it to the validator, increasing the validator's active stake once merged by update_validator_list_balance. Fails if a transient stake account already exists for the validator.

accounts.name: reserve_stake
constraints: must equal stake_pool.reserve_stake; must retain rent-exemption after funding

accounts.name: validator_stake
constraints: verified owned by the pool and delegated to given vote account

accounts.name: validator_vote
constraints: must match validator entry in list, status Active

cpis.description: create transient stake account
split from reserve into transient account; delegate_stake to validator vote account, signed by withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: Staker must sign; pool must be up to date; validator must be Active and not have a transient stake account already (else use Additional variant).
lamports must be at least minimum delegation; reserve must retain rent-exemption after funding lamports + stake rent.
validator_stake account must be verified as owned by the pool and delegated to the given vote account.

instructions.name: increase_additional_validator_stake
instructions.description: Increases stake on a validator again within the same epoch (even if a transient stake account already exists) by splitting reserve lamports into an ephemeral stake account, delegating it, then merging into the existing transient stake account.

accounts.name: transient_stake
constraints: if exists, seed must match recorded seed

accounts.name: validator_stake
constraints: verified delegated to vote account, status Active

cpis.description: create ephemeral stake account

split from reserve into ephemeral account; delegate_stake to vote account; merge ephemeral into transient (or create+split+delegate transient directly if none exists), signed by withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: Staker must sign; pool must be up to date; validator must be Active.
If transient stake already exists, the provided transient seed must match it.
lamports must be at least minimum delegation; reserve must retain sufficient rent-exempt balance.

instructions.name: set_preferred_validator
instructions.description: Sets or clears the preferred validator vote account that deposits (or withdrawals) must be directed to, restricting arbitrary rebalancing of stake between validators by depositors.
requirements: Staker must sign and match stake_pool.staker.
If setting a vote address, it must exist in validator_list with status Active, else the instruction fails.
Updates stake_pool.preferred_deposit_validator_vote_address or preferred_withdraw_validator_vote_address.

instructions.name: update_validator_list_balance
instructions.description: Recomputes and refreshes the recorded active/transient stake balances for a chunk of validators, merging matured transient stakes into the reserve or the corresponding validator stake account as appropriate.

accounts.name: validator_and_transient_stake_pairs
accounts.account_type: Remaining accounts: N pairs of (validator_stake, transient_stake)
constraints: pairs whose derived PDA addresses don't match the recorded validator entry are skipped; count must be even

cpis.description: merge (transient into reserve, transient into validator stake, or removed validator stake into reserve as applicable) and withdraw excess lamports on validator stake back to reserve, all signed by withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: The number of remaining accounts must be even (validator/transient pairs).
Pairs whose derived PDA addresses don't match the recorded validator entry are skipped.
Inactive transient stake is merged into the reserve; active transient stake with matching credits-observed merges into the validator stake account; otherwise balances are simply recorded.
Validator stake accounts pending removal that have fully deactivated are merged into the reserve and marked ReadyForRemoval (transient) or downgraded accordingly.
Each updated validator's last_update_epoch, active_stake_lamports and transient_stake_lamports are refreshed to the current epoch.
This instruction has no signer and can be called permissionlessly.

instructions.name: update_stake_pool_balance
instructions.description: Recomputes the stake pool's total lamports and pool token supply from the reserve and validator list, mints the manager's epoch fee in pool tokens, and rolls over any pending fee schedule changes.

accounts.name: validator_list
constraints: must equal stake_pool.validator_list, valid, program-owned; all entries must have last_update_epoch equal to current epoch

accounts.name: manager_fee_account
constraints: must equal stake_pool.manager_fee_account; if invalid, no fee is minted

cpis.description: mint_to manager_fee_account for the computed epoch fee, signed by withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: All validator_list entries must have last_update_epoch equal to the current epoch, else the call fails (must run update_validator_list_balance first).
manager_fee_account and pool_mint must match the stake pool's recorded accounts; if the fee account is invalid, no fee is minted (deposits/withdrawals are never blocked by this).
total_lamports and pool_token_supply are recomputed from the reserve, validator list, and mint supply.
On an epoch change, pending (FutureEpoch) fee updates for epoch/withdrawal fees advance one step and last_update_epoch, last_epoch_total_lamports, last_epoch_pool_token_supply are updated.
This instruction has no signer and can be called permissionlessly.

instructions.name: cleanup_removed_validator_entries
instructions.description: Removes validator entries marked ReadyForRemoval from the validator list, freeing space for new validators.
requirements: Only entries with status ReadyForRemoval are dropped; all others are retained.
This instruction has no signer and can be called permissionlessly.

instructions.name: deposit_stake
instructions.description: Merges a user-supplied, pool-authorized stake account into the corresponding validator stake account and mints pool tokens to the user (net of stake/SOL deposit fees and referral share) at the current exchange rate.

accounts.name: stake_deposit_authority
constraints: must equal stake_pool.stake_deposit_authority; must sign if it is not the program-derived default

accounts.name: stake_account
constraints: staker/withdrawer authority reassigned to withdraw_authority within the instruction

accounts.name: validator_stake_account
constraints: must match derived validator-stake PDA for the target validator; status must be Active; must match preferred deposit validator if set

signers: stake_deposit_authority (only if a custom, non-PDA authority is configured)

cpis.description: authorize (staker+withdrawer to withdraw-authority PDA), merge user's stake into validator stake account, withdraw any excess rent-exempt lamports back to reserve
mint_to user/manager-fee/referrer pool-token accounts

requirements: stake_deposit_authority must equal stake_pool.stake_deposit_authority and sign if it is not the program-derived default.
Pool must be up to date (last_update_epoch == current epoch).
The target validator must exist in validator_list with status Active and match the preferred deposit validator if one is set.

Pool tokens minted equal the (stake + any excess SOL) deposited, converted at the current ratio, minus stake/SOL deposit fee and minus referral fee share paid to the referrer; the remainder mints to the user.
The deposit must round to a nonzero number of pool tokens for the user (else DepositTooSmall).
validator_stake_info.active_stake_lamports and stake_pool.total_lamports/pool_token_supply are updated.

instructions.name: deposit_stake_with_slippage
instructions.description: Same as deposit_stake but requires the pool tokens minted to the user meet a caller-specified minimum, protecting against price movement.

cpis.description: same as deposit_stake
same as deposit_stake

requirements: Accounts are identical to deposit_stake.
All deposit_stake requirements apply.
Fails with ExceededSlippage if pool tokens credited to the user are below minimum_pool_tokens_out.

instructions.name: deposit_sol
instructions.description: Transfers SOL directly into the pool's reserve stake account and mints pool tokens to the user at the current exchange rate, net of SOL deposit fee and referral share.

accounts.name: sol_deposit_authority
constraints: must equal stake_pool.sol_deposit_authority and sign if set

cpis.description: transfer lamports_in from depositor to reserve
mint_to user/manager-fee/referrer pool-token accounts

requirements: If stake_pool.sol_deposit_authority is set, that account must sign and match.
Pool must be up to date.
Pool tokens minted to the user must be nonzero after fees (else DepositTooSmall).
stake_pool.total_lamports and pool_token_supply increase by the deposited amount and minted tokens respectively.

instructions.name: deposit_sol_with_slippage
instructions.description: Same as deposit_sol with an enforced minimum pool tokens to be received.

cpis.description: same as deposit_sol
same as deposit_sol

requirements: Accounts are identical to deposit_sol.
All deposit_sol requirements apply, plus fails with ExceededSlippage if under minimum_pool_tokens_out.

instructions.name: withdraw_stake
instructions.description: Burns the user's pool tokens and splits a stake account (from a validator, transient, or the reserve, in priority order) to a new stake account assigned to the user, deducting the pool's withdrawal fee.

accounts.name: stake_split_from
constraints: source priority: preferred withdraw validator, then active stake, then transient stake, then reserve or full validator removal; address checked against derived validator/transient/reserve PDA per case

accounts.name: user_stake_authority
constraints: becomes staker/withdrawer of the new stake account

cpis.description: burn pool tokens, transfer withdrawal-fee tokens to manager_fee_account
split stake_split_from into stake_split_to, authorize new stake+withdraw authority to user_stake_authority, signed by withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: Pool must be up to date.

Withdrawal source priority: preferred withdraw validator (if set and has withdrawable stake) > any validator with active stake above the tolerance > any validator with transient stake > the reserve or a full validator-removal withdrawal.

The resulting withdraw_lamports must be nonzero and, if withdrawing from an active/transient stake account, must leave the source at or above the required minimum, or exactly drain a validator being fully removed.

stake_pool.total_lamports and pool_token_supply decrease accordingly; the corresponding validator_list entry's active/transient lamports are decremented, and status becomes ReadyForRemoval if a validator account is fully drained.

instructions.name: withdraw_stake_with_slippage
instructions.description: Same as withdraw_stake but requires the lamports withdrawn to meet a caller-specified minimum.

cpis.description: same as withdraw_stake
same as withdraw_stake

requirements: Accounts are identical to withdraw_stake.
All withdraw_stake requirements apply, plus fails with ExceededSlippage if withdraw_lamports < minimum_lamports_out.

instructions.name: withdraw_sol
instructions.description: Burns the user's pool tokens and transfers SOL directly out of the reserve stake account to a destination system account, net of the SOL withdrawal fee.

accounts.name: reserve_stake
constraints: must equal stake_pool.reserve_stake; must remain at or above rent-exempt minimum after withdrawal

accounts.name: sol_withdraw_authority
constraints: must equal stake_pool.sol_withdraw_authority and sign if set

cpis.description: burn pool tokens, transfer withdrawal-fee tokens to manager_fee_account
withdraw lamports from reserve stake account to the destination, signed by withdraw-authority PDA

requirements: If stake_pool.sol_withdraw_authority is set, that account must sign and match.
Pool must be up to date.
withdraw_lamports must be nonzero, and the reserve must remain at or above its rent-exempt minimum after the withdrawal (else SolWithdrawalTooLarge).
stake_pool.total_lamports and pool_token_supply decrease accordingly.

instructions.name: withdraw_sol_with_slippage
instructions.description: Same as withdraw_sol but requires the lamports received to meet a caller-specified minimum.

cpis.description: same as withdraw_sol
same as withdraw_sol

requirements: Accounts are identical to withdraw_sol.
All withdraw_sol requirements apply, plus fails with ExceededSlippage if under minimum_lamports_out.

instructions.name: set_manager
instructions.description: Transfers the manager role and the manager fee-receiving token account to a new manager.

accounts.name: new_manager
constraints: proves control of the new key

accounts.name: new_manager_fee_account
constraints: owned by stake_pool.token_program_id; valid token account for pool_mint

requirements: Current manager must sign and match stake_pool.manager.
New manager must also sign (proves control of the new key).
new_manager_fee_account must be owned by the pool's token program and be a valid token account for the pool mint.
stake_pool.manager and manager_fee_account are updated.

instructions.name: set_fee
instructions.description: Updates one of the pool's fee parameters (referral %, epoch fee, stake/SOL deposit fee, stake/SOL withdrawal fee); withdrawal and epoch fees only take effect after a future epoch boundary.
requirements: Manager must sign and match stake_pool.manager.
For fee types that can only change next epoch (epoch fee, stake/SOL withdrawal fee), the pool must be up to date for the current epoch.
The new fee must not exceed 100% (numerator <= denominator).
Withdrawal fee increases are capped relative to the previous fee (or a baseline fee if previously zero) to protect stakers.
Epoch and withdrawal fee updates are staged via FutureEpoch and only become active after the required number of epoch boundaries; referral and deposit fee updates apply immediately.

instructions.name: set_staker
instructions.description: Transfers the staker role (validator/stake-management authority) to a new address; may be invoked by either the current staker or the manager.

accounts.name: set_staker_authority
constraints: must be either stake_pool.staker or stake_pool.manager

requirements: The signer must be either the current staker or the current manager.
stake_pool.staker is updated to new_staker.

instructions.name: set_funding_authority
instructions.description: Sets or clears the optional stake-deposit, SOL-deposit, or SOL-withdraw authority, controlling whether the pool is public (permissionless) or private (requires a co-signer) for that funding path.
requirements: Manager must sign and match stake_pool.manager.

For StakeDeposit, clearing (no new_authority) resets to the program-derived deposit-authority PDA (making stake deposits permissionless); for SolDeposit/SolWithdraw, clearing sets the authority to None (permissionless).

instructions.name: create_token_metadata
instructions.description: Creates a Metaplex token-metadata account for the pool's mint, recording its name/symbol/uri, with the pool's withdraw authority as both mint authority and metadata update authority.

accounts.name: metadata_account
constraints: must equal the Metaplex-derived metadata PDA for pool_mint

accounts.name: mpl_token_metadata_program
constraints: must be the expected Metaplex program id

cpis.description: create_metadata_accounts_v3, signed by the withdraw-authority PDA (as mint and update authority) and payer

requirements: payer must sign and be a system-owned account.
Manager must sign and match stake_pool.manager.
metadata_account address must equal the Metaplex-derived metadata PDA for pool_mint.
mpl_token_metadata_program must be the expected program id.

instructions.name: update_token_metadata
instructions.description: Updates the name/symbol/uri fields of the pool token's existing Metaplex metadata account.

accounts.name: metadata_account
constraints: must equal the Metaplex-derived metadata PDA for the pool's mint

accounts.name: mpl_token_metadata_program
constraints: must be the expected Metaplex program id

cpis.description: update_metadata_accounts_v2, signed by the withdraw-authority PDA (update authority)

requirements: Manager must sign and match stake_pool.manager.
metadata_account address must equal the Metaplex-derived metadata PDA for the pool's mint.

instructions.name: redelegate
instructions.description: (Deprecated, permanently disabled) Was intended to move stake directly from one validator to another via an ephemeral account; the handler unconditionally returns an error and performs no state change.
requirements: Always fails with InvalidInstructionData; the underlying stake-program redelegate instruction is not enabled and no CPI or state change is ever performed.

account_types: StakePool: main state account holding manager/staker pubkeys, mint, reserve, validator_list address, fee schedule (epoch/deposit/withdrawal fees + referral %, each with FutureEpoch pending updates), optional stake/SOL deposit & SOL withdraw authorities, preferred deposit/withdraw validators, total_lamports, pool_token_supply, last_update_epoch, lockup.
ValidatorList: header (account_type, max_validators) plus a growable Vec<ValidatorStakeInfo>, one entry per validator under management.

ValidatorStakeInfo: per-validator active_stake_lamports, transient_stake_lamports, last_update_epoch, transient/validator seed suffixes, StakeStatus (Active/DeactivatingTransient/DeactivatingValidator/DeactivatingAll/ReadyForRemoval), vote_account_address.
Reserve stake account: native Stake-program account whose staker/withdrawer authority is the pool's withdraw-authority PDA; holds undelegated SOL.
Validator stake account (PDA, seeds [vote, stake_pool, optional seed]): stake delegated to a specific validator, owned by the withdraw authority.
Transient stake account (PDA, seeds ["transient", vote, stake_pool, seed]): intermediate stake account used while activating/deactivating stake for a validator.
Ephemeral stake account (PDA, seeds ["ephemeral", stake_pool, seed]): short-lived stake account used to move stake without disturbing existing transient accounts.
Pool mint (external SPL Token/Token-2022 mint, mint authority = withdraw-authority PDA, no freeze authority).
Manager fee / user / referrer pool-token accounts (external SPL token accounts holding pool tokens).
Metaplex token-metadata account (external PDA derived from the pool mint) storing name/symbol/uri for the pool token.

components.name: Pool Initialization
components.description: Creation of a new stake pool: validating and wiring together the StakePool state, ValidatorList, reserve stake account, and pool mint before the pool becomes usable.

interactions.description: The manager signs pool creation and is recorded as the initial fee/config authority.
Mints initial pool tokens (if the reserve was pre-funded) and validates the pool mint/fee account.
The reserve stake account must already be an initialized stake account owned by this program.

requirements: Must atomically create and validate the StakePool and ValidatorList accounts, the reserve stake account, and the pool mint before the pool becomes usable.

components.name: Admin & Fee Configuration
components.description: Manager-controlled configuration of the pool: manager identity, fee schedule, and optional deposit/withdraw funding authorities.

interactions.description: Signs all administrative changes to fees, manager identity, and funding authorities.
May also reassign the staker role.

requirements: Only the manager may change manager identity, fees, or funding authorities; either manager or staker may reassign the staker.
Withdrawal fee increases are rate-limited and epoch/withdrawal-fee changes are staged for future epochs to protect stakers from surprise fee hikes.

components.name: Validator List Management
components.description: Staker-controlled membership of the validator set: adding, removing, and marking preferred validators, and pruning fully-removed entries.

interactions.description: Signs to add/remove validators and set preferred deposit/withdraw validators.
New validator stake accounts are created, delegated, and deactivated via CPI.
Deactivated/removed stake is later merged into the reserve by update_validator_list_balance, and cleanup_removed_validator_entries prunes fully-removed entries.

requirements: Only the staker may add/remove validators or set preferred validators.
A validator can only be added if the list has capacity and it is not already present; a validator can only be removed if currently Active.
Removed validators are only purged from the list once fully deactivated and merged (status ReadyForRemoval).

components.name: Stake Rebalancing
components.description: Staker-driven movement of stake between the reserve and individual validators, using transient and ephemeral stake accounts to activate or deactivate delegated stake.

interactions.description: Signs all rebalancing instructions.
Performs the underlying split/merge/delegate/deactivate/withdraw operations, signed by the pool's withdraw-authority PDA.
Allocates new transient/ephemeral stake accounts.
Transient and ephemeral stake movements are reconciled into recorded balances by update_validator_list_balance.

requirements: Only the staker may move stake between the reserve and validators.
Each validator may have at most one transient stake account at a time; 'Additional' instructions route through a fresh ephemeral account to make further adjustments within the same epoch.
All amounts must respect the stake program's minimum delegation and rent-exemption requirements.
redelegate is permanently disabled and always fails.

components.name: Balance Updates
components.description: Permissionless epoch-boundary reconciliation of per-validator and pool-wide stake balances, and collection of the manager's epoch management fee.

interactions.description: Merges and withdraws stake lamports between transient, validator, and reserve accounts.
Mints the epoch management fee to the manager's fee account.
Consumes the transient/ephemeral state produced by rebalancing instructions.
Finalizes removal of fully-deactivated validators (status transitions toward ReadyForRemoval).

requirements: Permissionless (no signer) instructions that must be run each epoch to refresh validator balances before update_stake_pool_balance, which requires all validator entries to be current.
update_stake_pool_balance mints the manager's epoch fee and advances any staged (FutureEpoch) fee changes.

components.name: Stake Deposits
components.description: Accepting user stake accounts into the pool by merging them into validator stake accounts and minting pool tokens in exchange.

interactions.description: Must sign if the pool is configured with a custom (private) stake deposit authority.
Reauthorizes and merges the user's stake account into the validator stake account, and withdraws excess lamports to the reserve.
Mints pool tokens to the user, manager fee account, and referrer.

requirements: Deposits must go to a validator with status Active and, if set, must match the pool's preferred deposit validator.
Requires either the program-derived deposit authority or a signing custom stake-deposit authority, depending on pool configuration.
Pool tokens minted must be nonzero and, for the slippage variant, must meet the caller's minimum.

components.name: SOL Deposits
components.description: Accepting direct SOL deposits into the pool's reserve stake account and minting pool tokens in exchange.

interactions.description: Must sign if the pool is configured with a custom (private) SOL deposit authority.
Transfers lamports from the depositor to the reserve.
Mints pool tokens to the user, manager fee account, and referrer.

requirements: Deposited lamports are transferred to the reserve stake account; pool tokens minted must be nonzero and, for the slippage variant, meet the caller's minimum.

components.name: Stake Withdrawals
components.description: Burning pool tokens to receive a stake account split from a validator, transient, or reserve stake account, following a defined withdrawal-source priority.

interactions.description: Signs to authorize burning the user's pool tokens.
Splits the source stake account and reassigns authority on the new stake account to the user.
Burns user pool tokens and transfers the withdrawal fee to the manager.

requirements: Withdrawal source must follow priority: preferred withdraw validator, then any validator with active stake, then transient stake, then the reserve or a full validator removal.
Burnt pool tokens and split lamports must satisfy the pool's fee, minimum-remaining-stake, and (for the slippage variant) minimum-lamports-out requirements.

components.name: SOL Withdrawals
components.description: Burning pool tokens to withdraw SOL directly from the pool's reserve stake account.

interactions.description: Must sign if the pool is configured with a custom (private) SOL withdraw authority.
Signs to authorize burning the user's pool tokens.
Withdraws lamports from the reserve stake account to the destination.
Burns user pool tokens and transfers the withdrawal fee to the manager.

requirements: Withdrawn lamports come directly from the reserve, which must remain at or above its rent-exempt minimum; for the slippage variant, must meet the caller's minimum lamports out.

components.name: Token Metadata
components.description: Manager-controlled creation and updating of the pool token's Metaplex on-chain metadata (name/symbol/uri).

interactions.description: Signs metadata creation/update.
Owns and processes the metadata account CPI.
Funds metadata account creation (via payer).

requirements: Only the manager may create or update the pool token's Metaplex metadata, using the withdraw-authority PDA as mint/update authority.

Stake_Rebalancing.description: Every rebalancing handler (increase_validator_stake, increase_additional_validator_stake, decrease_validator_stake, decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve, decrease_additional_validator_stake) must revert unless the `staker` account it is given both equals `stake_pool.staker` and is a signer; otherwise anyone can move pool stake between the reserve, validators and transient accounts at will.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: staker_signature_required_for_rebalancing

Stake_Rebalancing.description: Every rebalancing handler must revert when `stake_pool.last_update_epoch < clock.epoch`, because rebalancing against stale per-validator accounting lets the recorded active/transient lamports diverge from reality and be double-counted by the next UpdateValidatorListBalance.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: rebalancing_rejects_out_of_date_pool

Stake_Rebalancing.description: Every rebalancing handler must revert unless the stake_pool account is owned by this program with account_type == StakePool, the validator_list account is owned by this program with a valid header and a key equal to `stake_pool.validator_list`, and (for the handlers that take a reserve) the reserve account key equals `stake_pool.reserve_stake`; otherwise a look-alike pool/list/reserve can be substituted and pool bookkeeping written into an attacker-controlled account.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: rebalancing_validates_pool_list_and_reserve_identity

Stake_Rebalancing.description: Every rebalancing handler must revert unless the supplied withdraw_authority equals create_program_address([stake_pool, "withdraw", stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed], program_id), since this account is passed as the stake authority in every split/merge/delegate/deactivate/withdraw CPI that the pool signs with its PDA seeds.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: withdraw_authority_must_be_canonical_pda

Stake_Rebalancing.description: In every rebalancing handler the transient stake account must equal find_transient_stake_program_address(program_id, vote_account, stake_pool, transient_stake_seed) and, in the 'Additional' variants, the ephemeral stake account must equal find_ephemeral_stake_program_address(program_id, stake_pool, ephemeral_stake_seed) for the vote account bound to the validator list entry being updated; if the derivation is not re-checked, split stake is delivered into an account the caller controls.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: transient_and_ephemeral_accounts_must_be_canonical_pdas

Stake_Rebalancing.description: increase_validator_stake / increase_additional_validator_stake may split lamports only out of `stake_pool.reserve_stake` and only after verifying the validator stake account is stake-program-owned, at find_stake_program_address(program_id, vote, stake_pool, entry.validator_seed_suffix), with staker == withdrawer == the pool withdraw authority and lockup == stake_pool.lockup; the decrease handlers may split only out of an account whose address equals find_stake_program_address(program_id, vote, stake_pool, entry.validator_seed_suffix) where `vote` is the vote account recorded in that account's own delegation and a list entry for that vote account exists — otherwise pool-signed splits can be aimed at an unrelated stake account.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: stake_source_must_be_reserve_or_canonical_validator_stake

Stake_Rebalancing.description: If the targeted validator's list entry has transient_stake_lamports > 0 before the call, then increase_validator_stake and decrease_validator_stake(_with_reserve) must revert, and the 'Additional' variants must revert unless the supplied transient_stake_seed equals the entry's recorded transient_seed_suffix (leaving that suffix unchanged on success); violating this creates a second, untracked transient stake account per validator whose lamports UpdateValidatorListBalance will never reconcile.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: at_most_one_transient_stake_account_per_validator

Stake_Rebalancing.description: When a transient stake account already exists (transient_stake_lamports > 0), increase_additional_validator_stake must revert unless that account has deactivation_epoch == u64::MAX and activation_epoch == clock.epoch, and decrease_additional_validator_stake must revert unless it has deactivation_epoch == clock.epoch, so that activating and deactivating stake are never merged into a single transient account.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: additional_variants_require_matching_transient_state

Stake_Rebalancing.description: All four increase/decrease handlers must revert if the requested `lamports` is less than max(MINIMUM_ACTIVE_STAKE, the stake program's minimum delegation), otherwise the resulting transient/ephemeral stake account is below the merge-able minimum and its lamports become stranded.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: rebalance_amount_meets_minimum_delegation

Stake_Rebalancing.description: decrease_validator_stake, decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve and decrease_additional_validator_stake must revert unless, over exact integers, validator_stake.lamports - lamports >= meta.rent_exempt_reserve + max(MINIMUM_ACTIVE_STAKE, stake program minimum delegation), so a validator stake account is never left below the amount that permits future merges.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: decrease_leaves_validator_stake_above_minimum

Stake_Rebalancing.description: increase_validator_stake and increase_additional_validator_stake must revert unless, over exact integers, reserve.lamports - (lamports + stake rent-exemption) >= stake rent-exemption; in particular a `lamports` value for which lamports + stake_rent exceeds u64 must be rejected rather than saturating and splitting a different amount than the one recorded.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: increase_leaves_reserve_rent_exempt

Stake_Rebalancing.description: When decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve or decrease_additional_validator_stake funds the rent-exemption of a newly created transient or ephemeral stake account from the reserve, it must revert unless the reserve retains at least its own rent-exempt minimum afterwards; the present guard only rejects when the required top-up is >= the reserve's entire balance, so the reserve can be driven below rent exemption and reaped.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: decrease_must_not_drain_reserve_below_rent_exemption

Stake_Rebalancing.description: On a successful increase_validator_stake or increase_additional_validator_stake, the targeted validator entry's transient_stake_lamports increases by exactly `lamports + stake rent-exemption` over exact integers (no wrap, no saturation) and its active_stake_lamports is unchanged; a wrong delta mis-prices pool tokens at the next UpdateStakePoolBalance.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: increase_records_exact_transient_increase

Stake_Rebalancing.description: On a successful decrease_validator_stake, decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve or decrease_additional_validator_stake, the targeted validator entry's active_stake_lamports decreases by exactly `lamports` with no underflow or wraparound, so the pool never over- or under-reports the stake it still has delegated to that validator.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: decrease_records_exact_active_decrease

Stake_Rebalancing.description: No rebalancing handler may change the targeted list entry's vote_account_address, validator_seed_suffix, status or last_update_epoch, nor the validator list header (account_type, max_validators) or the number of entries, nor any byte of any other entry — checked over a bounded validator list of about three or four entries, since the list is a growable collection.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: rebalancing_preserves_entry_identity_and_other_entries

Stake_Rebalancing.description: No rebalancing handler may modify any field of the StakePool account — in particular total_lamports, pool_token_supply, last_update_epoch, staker, manager and the fee fields — since rebalancing only relocates stake among pool-owned accounts and must not move the pool token exchange rate.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: rebalancing_does_not_modify_stake_pool_account

Stake_Rebalancing.description: increase_validator_stake and increase_additional_validator_stake must revert if the targeted validator list entry's status is not Active, so stake is never sent to a validator already being removed where it would be stranded in a transient account of an entry heading for cleanup.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: increase_requires_active_validator

Stake_Rebalancing.description: The Redelegate instruction must always return an error regardless of the accounts and arguments supplied, and must leave the StakePool account, the ValidatorList account and all supplied stake account balances unchanged.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: redelegate_always_fails_without_state_change

Stake_Rebalancing.description: There exists an execution in which the correct signing staker, an up-to-date pool, an Active validator entry with no outstanding transient stake, canonical transient/validator-stake PDAs, a sufficiently funded reserve or validator stake account, and a `lamports` value at or above the minimum delegation makes increase_validator_stake and decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve succeed — i.e. the guards do not render rebalancing dead.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: legitimate_rebalance_is_reachable

Stake_Rebalancing.description: On every successful increase_additional_validator_stake and decrease_additional_validator_stake, the ephemeral stake account at PDA ["ephemeral", stake_pool, ephemeral_stake_seed] must be emptied into the validator's transient stake account — either by a stake-program merge whose source is the ephemeral account, or by a split whose lamport argument equals the ephemeral account's entire current balance (never a smaller amount derived from the `lamports` instruction argument) — because the ephemeral PDA is recorded in no field of StakePool or ValidatorList, so any residual lamports (including the rent-exemption top-up funded from the pool reserve) become pool funds that UpdateValidatorListBalance will never reconcile and that no accounting field reflects.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: ephemeral_stake_account_fully_drained_into_transient

Stake_Rebalancing.description: Spanning a two-instruction sequence in a single epoch: after increase_validator_stake succeeds in epoch E and records transient_seed_suffix = S with transient_stake_lamports > 0, a subsequent increase_additional_validator_stake in the same epoch E with transient_stake_seed = S, a canonical fresh ephemeral PDA, an Active validator entry and a sufficiently funded reserve must be able to succeed (and symmetrically decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve followed by decrease_additional_validator_stake); if the combined gates — the transient-seed equality check, check_if_stake_activating's requirement that the transient have activation_epoch == clock.epoch and deactivation_epoch == u64::MAX (resp. check_if_stake_deactivating's deactivation_epoch == clock.epoch), and the ephemeral PDA derivation — make this unreachable, the pool can be rebalanced at most once per validator per epoch and the 'Additional' instructions are dead code.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: same_epoch_additional_rebalance_is_reachable

Stake_Rebalancing.description: For every rebalancing handler, the total number of lamports it instructs the native stake program to split out of the pool's reserve stake account (increase_validator_stake, increase_additional_validator_stake) must equal exactly the amount it adds to the targeted validator entry's transient_stake_lamports, and the total number of lamports it instructs the stake program to split out of the validator stake account (decrease_validator_stake, decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve, decrease_additional_validator_stake) must equal exactly the amount it subtracts from that entry's active_stake_lamports — summed over every split CPI performed in the invocation, so that a rebalance never moves more or less real stake than it books; a mismatch makes the pool's recorded assets diverge from the stake it actually holds and mis-prices pool tokens at the next UpdateStakePoolBalance.
Stake_Rebalancing.title: rebalance_cpi_amount_matches_recorded_delta

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: process_set_manager must fail unless the `manager` account's key equals the pre-state stake_pool.manager and that account is a signer, AND the `new_manager` account is also a signer; otherwise anyone could seize the manager role and with it control of all fees, funding authorities and the fee-receiving token account.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_manager_requires_current_and_new_manager_signatures

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: process_set_fee must fail unless the `manager` account's key equals stake_pool.manager and that account is a signer; otherwise any caller could set a 100% deposit fee or stage a maximal withdrawal/epoch fee on the pool.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_fee_requires_manager_signature

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: process_set_staker must fail unless the `set_staker_authority` account is a signer and its key equals either stake_pool.staker or stake_pool.manager — key equality without `is_signer` must never suffice — otherwise anyone can take over the staker role that controls validator membership and stake rebalancing.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_staker_requires_signing_staker_or_manager

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: process_set_funding_authority must fail unless the `manager` account's key equals stake_pool.manager and that account is a signer; otherwise an attacker could clear sol_deposit_authority/sol_withdraw_authority (turning a private pool permissionless) or repoint stake_deposit_authority to a key they control.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_funding_authority_requires_manager_signature

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: Each of set_manager, set_fee, set_staker and set_funding_authority must fail if the stake_pool account's owner is not the executing program id, so that the manager/staker/token_program_id fields the handler trusts are never taken from an attacker-authored look-alike account.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: admin_handlers_require_program_owned_stake_pool

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: Each of set_manager, set_fee, set_staker and set_funding_authority must fail if the deserialized stake_pool.account_type is not AccountType::StakePool, so that manager, staker, fee or funding-authority values can never be written into a program-owned account that is uninitialized or holds a ValidatorList.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: admin_handlers_require_initialized_stake_pool

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: On a successful set_manager, stake_pool.manager equals the `new_manager` account key and stake_pool.manager_fee_account equals the `new_manager_fee_account` key, while staker, all three funding authorities and every fee field (active and staged) are unchanged; any other field write would be an unintended privilege or fee change smuggled through a manager handover.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_manager_updates_exactly_manager_and_fee_account

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: process_set_manager must fail unless the new manager fee account is owned by stake_pool.token_program_id, unpacks as an Initialized SPL token account whose mint equals stake_pool.pool_mint, and carries only supported token extensions; accepting a mismatched account makes the epoch-fee mint_to CPI in the balance-update path fail permanently, which bricks pool updates and therefore deposits and withdrawals.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_manager_validates_new_manager_fee_account

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: On a successful set_staker, stake_pool.staker equals the `new_staker` account key and manager, manager_fee_account, all funding authorities and all fee fields are unchanged; in particular a staker-initiated call must never be able to alter manager-only configuration.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_staker_updates_exactly_staker

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: On a successful set_funding_authority, exactly the field named by funding_type changes — set to the supplied optional authority account's key when one is passed and cleared (None, or the deposit PDA for StakeDeposit) when none is passed — and the other two funding-authority fields are untouched; a cross-write could silently clear sol_withdraw_authority and let anyone withdraw SOL from a private pool's reserve.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_funding_authority_updates_exactly_selected_authority

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: When set_funding_authority is called with funding_type StakeDeposit and no new-authority account, stake_pool.stake_deposit_authority must be set to the canonical program address derived from seeds [stake_pool_key, "deposit"] under the executing program id; a wrong derivation either permanently blocks stake deposits or, with wrong seeds, delegates deposit authorization to a foreign address.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_funding_authority_stake_deposit_clear_uses_canonical_pda

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: None of set_manager, set_fee, set_staker or set_funding_authority may modify stake_pool.total_lamports, pool_token_supply, last_update_epoch, last_epoch_pool_token_supply, last_epoch_total_lamports, validator_list, reserve_stake, pool_mint, token_program_id, stake_withdraw_bump_seed, account_type, lockup, or the preferred deposit/withdraw validator addresses; a write to any of them from an admin instruction would corrupt the pool's accounting or re-point it at a different mint, reserve or validator list.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: admin_handlers_preserve_pool_accounting_and_wiring

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: set_fee(f) must change exactly one fee slot: SolReferral/StakeReferral/SolDeposit/StakeDeposit write their corresponding active field, while Epoch/StakeWithdrawal/SolWithdrawal write only next_epoch_fee / next_stake_withdrawal_fee / next_sol_withdrawal_fee as FutureEpoch::Two(new) and must leave the corresponding *active* fee (and all other fee fields) unchanged — otherwise a manager could raise the fee actually charged to a user in the same block as that user's withdrawal.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_fee_modifies_exactly_the_selected_fee_slot

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: set_fee with FeeType::Epoch, StakeWithdrawal or SolWithdrawal must fail when stake_pool.last_update_epoch is less than the current clock epoch; staging a fee on a stale pool lets the still-pending balance update for the current epoch immediately count the value down from Two to One, halving the two-epoch notice period stakers are promised.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_fee_staged_types_require_pool_updated_this_epoch

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: set_fee with StakeWithdrawal or SolWithdrawal may succeed only if, over exact (unbounded) integer arithmetic, new_numerator * old_denominator * 2 <= old_numerator * new_denominator * 3, where (old_numerator, old_denominator) is the currently active corresponding withdrawal fee or (1, 1000) when that fee is zero; any accepted fee outside this bound is an unannounced withdrawal-fee hike on existing stakers.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: withdrawal_fee_increase_rate_limited

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: Fee::check_withdrawal compares two `Option<u128>` values built with `checked_mul(...).map(|x| x.checked_mul(...))`, and since Rust orders None below Some, an overflow of the right-hand product (new_numerator * old_denominator * 2) makes the comparison false and skips the cap entirely — so a manager can first stage a near-zero fee with a huge denominator (e.g. 1/(2^64-1), which passes the cap) and, once it is active, jump in a second set_fee call straight to 100% (e.g. 2^63/2^63); this attack spans a sequence of two set_fee calls separated by epoch boundaries.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: withdrawal_fee_cap_bypassed_by_u128_overflow_in_option_comparison

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: After any successful set_fee, every Fee value it wrote (active or staged) must satisfy numerator <= denominator and every referral percentage must be <= 100; a fee above 100% would charge a withdrawer more pool tokens than their withdrawal is worth, and a referral share above 100% would pay the referrer more than the whole collected deposit fee.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: set_fee_enforces_fee_at_most_one_hundred_percent

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: Given a signing manager, a program-owned initialized pool that is up to date for the current epoch, and a proposed withdrawal fee whose ratio is no greater than the currently active one (with fee denominators bounded, e.g. below 2^32, to exclude u128 overflow), set_fee with StakeWithdrawal or SolWithdrawal must succeed; if it can fail, the rate-limit guard is over-strict and stakers are permanently locked into the existing fee.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: withdrawal_fee_decrease_is_always_permitted

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: Each of set_manager, set_fee, set_staker and set_funding_authority must leave the lamport balance of every account it is passed exactly unchanged and must write data to no account other than `stake_pool` — in particular set_manager must not write into `new_manager_fee_account`, and none of the four may debit the pool account below rent exemption or move value on behalf of any signer; a violation would corrupt a user/manager token account or strip lamports from the pool during what is meant to be a pure configuration write.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: admin_handlers_touch_only_stake_pool_account

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: Because StakePool is Borsh-encoded with variable-length fields (`next_epoch_fee`, `next_stake_withdrawal_fee`, `next_sol_withdrawal_fee` occupy 1 byte as FutureEpoch::None but 17 as Two(fee), and `sol_deposit_authority`/`sol_withdraw_authority` occupy 1 byte as None but 33 as Some) while `process_initialize` validates only rent-exemption and never that the stake_pool account's data length can hold the maximum-size encoding, a pool whose account was sized to its initial all-None encoding can reach a state where set_fee with FeeType::Epoch/StakeWithdrawal/SolWithdrawal and set_funding_authority with SolDeposit/SolWithdraw and an authority account can never succeed, because the final `borsh::to_writer(&mut stake_pool_info.data.borrow_mut()[..], ..)` runs out of slice; the consequence is that the pool's fee schedule and its public/private funding toggle become permanently immutable — including the inability to ever *lower* an epoch or withdrawal fee that was initialized high.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: staged_fee_write_blocked_by_undersized_stake_pool_account

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: Given a program-owned stake_pool with account_type StakePool whose account data is large enough for the maximum StakePool encoding: set_manager must succeed when the stored manager and the new manager both sign and `new_manager_fee_account` is an extension-free, Initialized SPL token account of `stake_pool.pool_mint` owned by `stake_pool.token_program_id`; set_staker must succeed when the stored manager signs; and set_funding_authority with FundingType::StakeDeposit must succeed when the stored manager signs — if any of these guards can reject such a call, the manager, staker or stake-deposit-authority role becomes permanently untransferable, since no other authority in the program can repair it.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: admin_role_transfer_is_always_reachable_for_signing_manager

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: No instruction handler other than initialize, set_manager, set_staker and set_funding_authority may change the stake_pool account's manager, manager_fee_account, staker, stake_deposit_authority, sol_deposit_authority or sol_withdraw_authority fields — this must hold in particular for the eight non-admin handlers that deserialize and re-serialize the whole StakePool record (remove_validator_from_pool, set_preferred_validator, update_stake_pool_balance, deposit_stake, deposit_sol, withdraw_stake, withdraw_sol and their slippage variants) as well as every read-only handler; because several of those handlers are permissionless (deposit_sol, withdraw_sol, update_stake_pool_balance) or only staker-authorized, a stray write there would let a non-manager seize the manager or staker role, repoint the fee-receiving token account, or clear sol_withdraw_authority and turn a private pool's reserve into a permissionless one.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: admin_roles_and_funding_authorities_only_writable_by_admin_handlers

Admin_Fee_Configuration.description: No instruction handler other than initialize, set_fee and update_stake_pool_balance may change any of epoch_fee, stake_deposit_fee, sol_deposit_fee, stake_withdrawal_fee, sol_withdrawal_fee, stake_referral_fee, sol_referral_fee, next_epoch_fee, next_stake_withdrawal_fee or next_sol_withdrawal_fee, and update_stake_pool_balance may only advance the three staged FutureEpoch slots and copy an activated staged value into its own corresponding active epoch/withdrawal fee — never touching the deposit or referral fees; otherwise a permissionless deposit/withdraw handler could rewrite the fee schedule without the manager, or a staged withdrawal fee could become the fee actually charged on a path other than the promised two-epoch countdown.
Admin_Fee_Configuration.title: fee_schedule_only_writable_by_set_fee_and_the_epoch_countdown

Validator_List_Management.description: add_validator_to_pool, remove_validator_from_pool and set_preferred_validator must all abort unless the supplied staker account both equals stake_pool.staker and is a signer of the transaction; otherwise anyone could insert, deactivate or re-target validators in the pool's validator set.
Validator_List_Management.title: staker_signature_required_for_list_mutation

Validator_List_Management.description: Each of add_validator_to_pool, remove_validator_from_pool, set_preferred_validator and cleanup_removed_validator_entries must abort unless the passed validator_list account key equals stake_pool.validator_list, both the stake_pool and validator_list accounts are owned by this program, stake_pool.account_type is StakePool and the list header account_type is ValidatorList — otherwise a caller (cleanup takes no signer at all) can substitute a look-alike list account they control and have the program mutate or prune arbitrary data.
Validator_List_Management.title: validator_list_bound_to_stake_pool

Validator_List_Management.description: add_validator_to_pool and remove_validator_from_pool must abort unless the supplied withdraw_authority account equals the program address derived from [stake_pool, "withdraw"] with stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed, because that account (and that bump) is used as the invoke_signed authority for splitting reserve lamports and deactivating stake; a substituted authority would let stake be moved under a key the pool does not control.
Validator_List_Management.title: withdraw_authority_pda_validated_before_cpi_signing

Validator_List_Management.description: add_validator_to_pool and remove_validator_from_pool must abort when stake_pool.last_update_epoch is less than the current clock epoch, so that validator entries are never added to or marked on a list whose per-validator balances are stale relative to the pool's total_lamports accounting.
Validator_List_Management.title: list_mutation_requires_pool_updated_this_epoch

Validator_List_Management.description: On a successful add_validator_to_pool the validator list length increases by exactly one, the appended entry has status Active, vote_account_address equal to the passed validator_vote account, transient_stake_lamports 0, transient_seed_suffix 0, last_update_epoch equal to the current epoch and validator_seed_suffix equal to the seed argument, and every pre-existing entry is left byte-for-byte unchanged; any deviation silently corrupts another validator's recorded stake.
Validator_List_Management.title: add_validator_appends_exactly_one_active_entry

Validator_List_Management.description: The active_stake_lamports recorded on the entry appended by add_validator_to_pool must equal max(stake program minimum delegation, MINIMUM_ACTIVE_STAKE) plus the rent-exempt minimum for a StakeStateV2 account — exactly the amount requested in the split from the reserve — so that the list's recorded stake never diverges from the lamports actually moved out of the reserve.
Validator_List_Management.title: add_validator_records_exactly_the_funded_amount

Validator_List_Management.description: add_validator_to_pool must abort if any entry already in the list carries the same vote_account_address, so that in every reachable state no two validator list entries share a vote account; duplicates would double-count stake and make lookups by vote address (used by deposit, withdraw, remove and rebalancing) resolve to the wrong entry. Checking the post-state requires a bounded list (e.g. up to 4 entries).
Validator_List_Management.title: validator_list_vote_accounts_are_unique

Validator_List_Management.description: add_validator_to_pool must abort when the list length already equals the header's max_validators, and after a successful call the length must still be at most max_validators, so entries can never be pushed past the region the account was sized and accounted for.
Validator_List_Management.title: add_validator_respects_max_validators_capacity

Validator_List_Management.description: add_validator_to_pool must abort unless the passed stake account address equals the program address derived from [validator_vote, stake_pool, seed] (seed omitted when the u32 seed argument is 0), and the account-creation CPI must be signed with exactly those seeds and the canonical bump; without this the staker could have reserve lamports split into an arbitrary account.
Validator_List_Management.title: add_validator_validates_new_stake_account_pda

Validator_List_Management.description: add_validator_to_pool must abort unless the reserve account is stake_pool.reserve_stake and its lamports minus the amount to be split still leave at least the reserve's rent-exempt reserve, so funding a new validator can never drop the reserve stake account below rent exemption.
Validator_List_Management.title: add_validator_preserves_reserve_rent_exemption

Validator_List_Management.description: A successful add_validator_to_pool must leave every field of the StakePool account unchanged (it only appends to the validator list and moves lamports between pool-owned stake accounts); any write to the pool here would be a covert configuration or accounting change.
Validator_List_Management.title: add_validator_does_not_modify_stake_pool_state

Validator_List_Management.description: remove_validator_from_pool must abort unless the validator list entry matching the vote account read from the stake account's delegation has status exactly Active; otherwise an entry already in a Deactivating* or ReadyForRemoval state could be pushed back to a 'deactivating' status, resurrecting an entry whose stake has already been merged into the reserve and double-counting it.
Validator_List_Management.title: remove_validator_requires_active_entry

Validator_List_Management.description: A successful remove_validator_from_pool leaves the validator list length unchanged and modifies only the status byte of the matched entry (to DeactivatingValidator or DeactivatingAll), leaving that entry's active/transient lamports, seed suffixes and vote address and every other entry unchanged — deleting or rewriting accounting fields here would strand stake that has not yet been merged back into the reserve.
Validator_List_Management.title: remove_validator_marks_but_never_deletes_entry

Validator_List_Management.description: remove_validator_from_pool must abort unless the supplied stake account address equals the validator-stake PDA derived from the vote account in its own delegation, the stake pool and the entry's recorded validator_seed_suffix, and — whenever the entry records transient_stake_lamports greater than zero — unless the supplied transient account equals the transient-stake PDA for that vote account and the entry's transient_seed_suffix; otherwise unrelated accounts could be deactivated under the pool's withdraw authority or one validator marked for removal using another's stake account.
Validator_List_Management.title: remove_validator_binds_stake_accounts_to_the_entry

Validator_List_Management.description: After a successful remove_validator_from_pool, neither stake_pool.preferred_deposit_validator_vote_address nor preferred_withdraw_validator_vote_address may equal the removed validator's vote account, and no other StakePool field may change; a leftover preference pins deposits or withdrawals to a validator that is leaving the pool and blocks them.
Validator_List_Management.title: remove_validator_clears_preferred_reference

Validator_List_Management.description: When remove_validator_from_pool is called on an entry that records transient_stake_lamports greater than zero and the supplied transient account is a stake account usable by the pool (authorities equal to the withdraw authority and matching lockup), the resulting status must be DeactivatingAll rather than DeactivatingValidator, so that the transient stake is still tracked and later merged into the reserve instead of being forgotten while its lamports remain recorded.
Validator_List_Management.title: remove_validator_status_accounts_for_transient_stake

Validator_List_Management.description: set_preferred_validator with a Some(vote) argument must abort unless the validator list contains an entry with that vote account whose status is Active, and on success the corresponding preferred field must equal exactly that vote account; allowing a missing or deactivating validator to be set as preferred would immediately block all deposits (or withdrawals) routed through the preference check.
Validator_List_Management.title: set_preferred_validator_requires_active_listed_entry

Validator_List_Management.description: set_preferred_validator with validator_type Deposit must leave preferred_withdraw_validator_vote_address and every other StakePool field unchanged, and symmetrically for Withdraw, so that a single preference update cannot covertly alter the other routing preference or any pool configuration.
Validator_List_Management.title: set_preferred_validator_touches_only_the_selected_field

Validator_List_Management.description: The staker must always be able to clear a preference by calling set_preferred_validator with None, regardless of the contents or state of the validator list; if the clearing path were gated on the listed entry existing or being Active, a pool whose preferred validator has been removed could never have deposits or withdrawals unblocked again.
Validator_List_Management.title: set_preferred_validator_can_always_clear

Validator_List_Management.description: After a successful cleanup_removed_validator_entries the validator list must equal the pre-state list with exactly the entries whose status is ReadyForRemoval removed — remaining entries preserved byte-for-byte and in their original relative order, and the length field decreased by exactly the number of dropped entries; BigVec::retain does this with unsafe sol_memmove and hand-written index arithmetic, so an off-by-one would silently delete or corrupt live validators' recorded stake. Checking this requires bounding the list (e.g. up to 4 entries).
Validator_List_Management.title: cleanup_drops_exactly_the_ready_for_removal_entries

Validator_List_Management.description: Any validator list entry whose status is ReadyForRemoval must have both active_stake_lamports and transient_stake_lamports equal to zero; this is what makes the permissionless cleanup_removed_validator_entries safe, and each handler of this component (add sets Active with the funded amount, remove sets only Deactivating* statuses, cleanup only drops entries) must preserve it — if it were violated, cleanup would silently discard lamports that are still counted in the pool's totals.
Validator_List_Management.title: ready_for_removal_entries_record_no_stake

Validator_List_Management.description: cleanup_removed_validator_entries drops ReadyForRemoval entries without consulting stake_pool.preferred_deposit_validator_vote_address / preferred_withdraw_validator_vote_address, while the full-validator-removal path of WithdrawStake sets an entry to ReadyForRemoval without clearing those fields, so after cleanup the pool can reference a vote account that no longer has a list entry — after which every DepositStake fails with ValidatorNotFound until the staker resets the preference; the property to check is that after cleanup, any Some(vote) preference still resolves to an entry in the list.
Validator_List_Management.title: cleanup_can_orphan_a_preferred_validator_reference

Validator_List_Management.description: With a valid stake_pool and its matching validator_list and no signer at all, cleanup_removed_validator_entries must succeed and actually shorten a list containing at least one ReadyForRemoval entry; if the guards were strict enough to make it unreachable, dead entries would permanently consume the pool's max_validators capacity and no new validator could ever be added.
Validator_List_Management.title: cleanup_is_permissionless_and_frees_capacity

Validator_List_Management.description: When the staker signs and equals stake_pool.staker, the stake_pool is program-owned with account_type StakePool and last_update_epoch >= clock.epoch, the validator_list is program-owned, header-valid, equal to stake_pool.validator_list, has len < max_validators and contains no entry for the passed validator_vote, the passed stake account key equals find_stake_program_address(validator_vote, stake_pool, seed), the reserve equals stake_pool.reserve_stake and holds at least its rent-exempt reserve plus max(MINIMUM_ACTIVE_STAKE, stake-program minimum delegation) plus the StakeStateV2 rent-exempt minimum, and the system/stake program ids and rent/clock sysvars are canonical, then add_validator_to_pool must succeed and the validator list length must increase by exactly one; if any guard is stricter than this the pool can never onboard a validator and, once capacity is consumed, is permanently stuck.
Validator_List_Management.title: add_validator_to_pool_is_reachable_for_the_staker

Validator_List_Management.description: When the staker signs and equals stake_pool.staker, the stake_pool is program-owned, valid and up to date for the current epoch, the validator_list matches stake_pool.validator_list and is header-valid, the passed stake_account sits at the validator-stake PDA derived from the vote account recorded in its own delegation and the matching entry's validator_seed_suffix, that entry has status Active, and (when the entry records transient_stake_lamports > 0) the passed transient account sits at the derived transient-stake PDA, then remove_validator_from_pool must succeed and set that entry's status to DeactivatingValidator or DeactivatingAll; if removal can be blocked in this state the pool's stake stays delegated to a validator it wants out of and the list slot is never freed for a replacement.
Validator_List_Management.title: remove_validator_from_pool_is_reachable_for_an_active_validator

Validator_List_Management.description: add_validator_to_pool, remove_validator_from_pool and cleanup_removed_validator_entries must leave the validator list account's header bytes — account_type and max_validators — byte-for-byte identical before and after, touching only the 4-byte length prefix and the entry region; BigVec::push writes at a hand-computed index and BigVec::retain compacts entries with raw sol_memmove over hand-computed offsets, so an off-by-one that walked backwards would silently rewrite max_validators (changing the pool's apparent capacity) or account_type (making every subsequent header.is_valid() check fail and permanently bricking every instruction that reads the list).
Validator_List_Management.title: validator_list_header_never_mutated_by_list_handlers

Validator_List_Management.description: When the staker signs and equals stake_pool.staker, the stake_pool account is program-owned with account_type StakePool, the validator_list equals stake_pool.validator_list, is program-owned and header-valid and contains an entry for vote account v with status Active, then set_preferred_validator(Deposit|Withdraw, Some(v)) must succeed and leave the corresponding preferred_*_validator_vote_address equal to Some(v) — in particular the handler's final write-back of the whole StakePool must fit in the stake_pool account even though switching a preference from None to Some grows the borsh encoding by 32 bytes; if it cannot, the pool can never pin deposits or withdrawals to a chosen validator and permanently loses that routing control.
Validator_List_Management.title: set_preferred_validator_can_actually_set_a_preference

Pool_Initialization.description: The `Initialize` handler must fail unless the `manager` account (account index 1) has `is_signer == true`; otherwise anyone could create a pool that names an arbitrary, non-consenting key as manager and thereby as the permanent fee/config authority.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_requires_manager_signature
