Pool_Initialization.description: If the `stake_pool` account passed to `Initialize` is not owned by this program, or its deserialized `account_type` is anything other than `Uninitialized`, the handler must fail and leave every byte of that account unchanged; otherwise a live pool could be re-initialized, resetting manager/staker/fees and resetting `total_lamports` and `pool_token_supply` to the reserve's excess while pool tokens are still outstanding — an arbitrary seizure of the entire pool.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_rejects_already_initialized_stake_pool

Pool_Initialization.description: If the `validator_list` account passed to `Initialize` is not owned by this program, or its header `account_type` is anything other than `Uninitialized`, the handler must fail; otherwise an existing pool's validator list could be cleared, erasing the accounting for every validator stake account the pool holds.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_rejects_already_initialized_validator_list

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` must fail when the `stake_pool` and `validator_list` accounts are the same account, because the handler serializes both structures into that one buffer and the second write silently clobbers the first, yielding a single account that other handlers would read as both a StakePool and a ValidatorList.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_rejects_pool_aliased_with_validator_list

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` may succeed only if the supplied `withdraw_authority` account key equals `find_program_address([stake_pool_key, "withdraw"], program_id).0`, and on success `stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed` must be exactly that canonical bump; recording an attacker-chosen authority or a non-canonical bump would make every later instruction that signs as the pool's withdraw authority (mint, burn, stake split/withdraw) validate against the wrong address.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_binds_canonical_withdraw_authority_pda

Pool_Initialization.description: On a successful `Initialize`, `stake_pool.manager`, `.staker`, `.validator_list`, `.reserve_stake`, `.pool_mint`, `.manager_fee_account` and `.token_program_id` must equal the keys of the `manager`, `staker`, `validator_list`, `reserve_stake`, `pool_mint`, `manager_fee_account` and `token_program` accounts actually passed in, since every later instruction authenticates its accounts against these stored keys and any mismatch is a permanent account-substitution vector.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_records_exactly_the_passed_accounts

Pool_Initialization.description: On a successful `Initialize`, `stake_pool.total_lamports` and `stake_pool.pool_token_supply` must both equal exactly `reserve_stake.lamports - meta.rent_exempt_reserve - MINIMUM_RESERVE_LAMPORTS` computed over exact integers, and the amount passed to the `mint_to` CPI must equal that same value (with the CPI omitted when the value is zero); any divergence between the minted supply and the recorded `pool_token_supply` sets the pool's exchange rate wrong at genesis and mis-prices every subsequent deposit and withdrawal.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_mints_exactly_the_reserve_excess

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` must fail if any of `fee`, `withdrawal_fee` or `deposit_fee` has `numerator > denominator`, or if `referral_fee > 100`, and on success the stored `epoch_fee`, `stake_deposit_fee`, `sol_deposit_fee`, `stake_withdrawal_fee`, `sol_withdrawal_fee`, `stake_referral_fee` and `sol_referral_fee` must equal the supplied arguments; a fee above 100% lets the manager capture more than the entire deposit or withdrawal.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_rejects_fees_above_one

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` must fail unless `max_validators > 0` and `ValidatorList::calculate_max_validators(validator_list.data_len()) == max_validators`, and on success `validator_list.header.max_validators` must equal the `max_validators` argument; a header claiming more capacity than the buffer physically holds lets later `AddValidatorToPool` calls write entries the account cannot store.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_validator_list_size_matches_max_validators

Pool_Initialization.description: On a successful `Initialize`, the `validator_list` account must have `header.account_type == ValidatorList` and a serialized validator vector of length 0, regardless of the account's prior byte contents; otherwise entries pre-seeded by whoever funded the account would be treated as real validators with attacker-chosen vote accounts and balances.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_validator_list_starts_empty_and_typed

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` must fail unless the `reserve_stake` account is owned by the native stake program, deserializes as `StakeStateV2::Initialized(meta)`, has `meta.lockup == Lockup::default()`, and has both `meta.authorized.staker` and `meta.authorized.withdrawer` equal to the pool's withdraw-authority PDA; otherwise circulating pool tokens would be backed by a reserve that is locked up or still controlled by a third party, and SOL withdrawals would be unserviceable.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_rejects_invalid_reserve_stake

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` must fail unless the `pool_mint` account is owned by the supplied `token_program`, has supply 0, has 9 decimals, has `mint_authority` equal to the pool's withdraw-authority PDA, and has no freeze authority; a nonzero pre-existing supply means unbacked tokens exist from block zero, and a foreign mint or freeze authority lets a third party inflate or freeze the pool token.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_rejects_invalid_pool_mint

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` must fail unless the `manager_fee_account` is owned by the recorded `token_program_id`, is in `Initialized` state, and has `mint == pool_mint`; otherwise the genesis mint and all later fee payments would target a token account of a different mint, or the fee-minting CPI would fail permanently.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_rejects_foreign_manager_fee_account

Pool_Initialization.description: On a successful `Initialize`, `stake_pool.token_program_id` must be one of the two accepted SPL token program ids and must equal `pool_mint.owner`, and the only CPI the handler performs is a `mint_to` to that pinned program; if an arbitrary account could be recorded as the token program, every subsequent mint/burn/transfer CPI made by the pool would be a call into attacker-controlled code.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_pins_token_program

Pool_Initialization.description: On a successful `Initialize`, if an optional tenth account is supplied then `stake_pool.stake_deposit_authority` equals its key and `stake_pool.sol_deposit_authority == Some(that key)`, and if it is absent then `stake_pool.stake_deposit_authority == find_program_address([stake_pool_key, "deposit"], program_id).0` and `stake_pool.sol_deposit_authority == None`; in both cases `stake_pool.sol_withdraw_authority == None`. Getting this wrong silently makes a pool that should be permissioned open to anyone, or permanently gates all deposits behind a key nobody holds.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_optional_deposit_authority_semantics

Pool_Initialization.description: If the optional deposit-authority account is supplied to `Initialize`, it must have `is_signer == true`; the handler currently reads the tenth account with `next_account_info` and records it as both `stake_deposit_authority` and `sol_deposit_authority` without ever checking `is_signer`, so a pool can be created whose configured funding authority never demonstrated key ownership, contrary to the stated account requirements.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_deposit_authority_must_sign

Pool_Initialization.description: On a successful `Initialize`, every field of the resulting `StakePool` must be a function only of the instruction arguments, the passed accounts and the clock, with no field retaining a value from the account's prior data — in particular `sol_withdraw_authority == None`, both preferred-validator fields `== None`, `next_epoch_fee`/`next_stake_withdrawal_fee`/`next_sol_withdrawal_fee == FutureEpoch::None`, `lockup == Lockup::default()`, and `last_epoch_pool_token_supply == last_epoch_total_lamports == 0`; because the handler deserializes the existing bytes and assigns fields one by one, a single missed field would let whoever pre-wrote the account plant e.g. a `sol_withdraw_authority` they control or a pending fee change.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_overwrites_all_stake_pool_fields

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` must either fail leaving both the `stake_pool` and `validator_list` accounts byte-for-byte unchanged, or succeed with `stake_pool.account_type == StakePool`, `validator_list.header.account_type == ValidatorList` and `stake_pool.validator_list == validator_list.key`; a half-activated outcome would leave a pool that other handlers accept as valid while its validator list is untyped or points elsewhere.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_atomically_activates_both_accounts

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` must fail unless both the `stake_pool` and the `validator_list` accounts hold at least the rent-exempt minimum for their current data length, since a non-exempt state account can be reaped by the runtime while pool tokens circulate, stranding the staked funds and freeing the address for re-initialization.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_requires_rent_exemption

Pool_Initialization.description: There must exist an input to `Initialize` — manager signing, stake pool and validator list program-owned, uninitialized, rent-exempt and correctly sized for a nonzero `max_validators`, all fees at most 1, a zero-supply 9-decimal mint with the withdraw-authority PDA as mint authority and no freeze authority, a matching manager fee account, and an initialized unlocked reserve stake authorized to the withdraw PDA — on which the handler succeeds and sets `stake_pool.account_type == StakePool`; if no such input exists the guards are mutually contradictory and no pool can ever be created.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_happy_path_reachable

Pool_Initialization.description: For any stake_pool account whose `account_type` is `StakePool`, no instruction handler other than `Initialize` may change `account_type`, `validator_list`, `reserve_stake`, `pool_mint`, `token_program_id` or `stake_withdraw_bump_seed`, and no handler may change the validator list's `header.account_type` or `header.max_validators` — checked across AddValidatorToPool, RemoveValidatorFromPool, SetPreferredValidator, CleanupRemovedValidatorEntries, Increase/DecreaseValidatorStake (and their Additional/WithReserve variants), UpdateValidatorListBalance, UpdateStakePoolBalance, DepositStake(WithSlippage), WithdrawStake(WithSlippage), DepositSol(WithSlippage), WithdrawSol(WithSlippage), SetManager, SetStaker, SetFee, SetFundingAuthority and Create/UpdateTokenMetadata; if any of them could re-point the pool at a different validator list, reserve stake account, mint or token program, the manager or staker could swap out the pool's entire backing after users have deposited, and a mutated `stake_withdraw_bump_seed` would invalidate every `check_authority_withdraw` and every `invoke_signed` the pool performs.
Pool_Initialization.title: pool_identity_fields_are_write_once_after_initialize

Pool_Initialization.description: No instruction handler may reduce the lamports of, shrink/zero the data of, or otherwise close the `stake_pool` account or the `validator_list` account, so that for any given stake_pool address (and any given validator_list address) at most one `Initialize` can ever succeed no matter the sequence of instructions; if a close-and-recreate path existed, anyone could re-run `Initialize` on a live pool's address and reset manager, staker, fees, `total_lamports` and `pool_token_supply` while pool tokens are still outstanding. This property spans a sequence (close, then re-initialize) and is the cross-handler complement to Initialize's own `Uninitialized` guard.
Pool_Initialization.title: state_accounts_are_never_closed_so_initialize_is_one_shot

Pool_Initialization.description: `Initialize` must fail unless every Token-2022 extension present on the `pool_mint` account is in the supported set (Uninitialized, TransferFeeConfig, ConfidentialTransferMint, ConfidentialTransferFeeConfig, DefaultAccountState, InterestBearingConfig, MetadataPointer, TokenMetadata) — in particular it must reject a mint carrying PermanentDelegate, MintCloseAuthority, TransferHook or NonTransferable — because `pool_mint` is recorded immutably at initialization and is never re-validated by any later handler, so a permanent delegate could burn or seize every holder's pool tokens for the life of the pool, a mint close authority could destroy the mint, and a transfer hook would inject third-party code into every pool-token movement.
Pool_Initialization.title: initialize_rejects_pool_mint_with_unsupported_extensions

Pool_Initialization.description: Every instruction handler other than Initialize must reject its stake_pool account unless that account is owned by this program AND its deserialized account_type is exactly AccountType::StakePool, and must reject its validator_list account (when it takes one) unless that account is owned by this program AND its header account_type is exactly AccountType::ValidatorList — checked across AddValidatorToPool, RemoveValidatorFromPool, SetPreferredValidator, CleanupRemovedValidatorEntries, IncreaseValidatorStake, IncreaseAdditionalValidatorStake, DecreaseValidatorStake, DecreaseValidatorStakeWithReserve, DecreaseAdditionalValidatorStake, UpdateValidatorListBalance, UpdateStakePoolBalance, DepositStake(WithSlippage), WithdrawStake(WithSlippage), DepositSol(WithSlippage), WithdrawSol(WithSlippage), SetManager, SetStaker, SetFee, SetFundingAuthority and Create/UpdateTokenMetadata; because this is a native program with no Anchor Account<T> to check ownership for it, omitting the owner check would let an attacker pass a look-alike account created under a program they control, carrying an attacker-chosen manager, staker, reserve_stake, pool_mint, manager_fee_account, token_program_id and stake_withdraw_bump_seed, and omitting the account_type gate would let a freshly allocated all-zero program-owned account be driven as if it were a live pool — either way the handler acts on a pool that Initialize never validated, which is precisely the state this component exists to prevent.
Pool_Initialization.title: pool_unusable_until_initialized

Pool_Initialization.description: Every instruction handler must authenticate the auxiliary accounts it is given against the keys that Initialize recorded in the StakePool — validator_list_info.key == stake_pool.validator_list, reserve_stake_info.key == stake_pool.reserve_stake (wherever the reserve is a required rather than branch-selecting account; WithdrawStake deliberately treats its stake_split_from as polymorphic and only compares it to decide the source), pool_mint_info.key == stake_pool.pool_mint, token_program_info.key == stake_pool.token_program_id, manager_fee_info.key == stake_pool.manager_fee_account, and withdraw_authority_info.key == create_program_address([stake_pool.key, "withdraw", stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed], program_id) — and must fail otherwise; since the ValidatorList carries no back-pointer to its pool and the reserve stake account carries no pool identifier, these stored keys are the only thing binding a pool to its backing accounts, so a handler that skipped one would let an attacker feed pool A's validator list, reserve stake, mint or fee account into an instruction operating on pool B, corrupting another pool's per-validator accounting, moving another pool's reserve lamports, minting or burning the wrong token, or redirecting fee tokens, and a missing token_program_id comparison would turn every mint/burn/transfer into an arbitrary CPI into attacker-controlled code.
Pool_Initialization.title: handlers_bind_accounts_to_recorded_pool_fields

Balance_Updates.description: update_validator_list_balance may modify only the active_stake_lamports, transient_stake_lamports, last_update_epoch and status fields of validator-list entries in the index range [start_index, start_index + number_of_account_pairs); every entry outside that range, the vote_account_address / validator_seed_suffix / transient_seed_suffix of every entry, the list length and the list header must be unchanged, otherwise a permissionless caller could clobber other validators' recorded balances or rewrite the vote-account-to-stake-PDA mapping.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_only_touches_selected_entries_and_fields

Balance_Updates.description: If the (validator_stake, transient_stake) pair supplied for a validator-list entry does not derive exactly to find_stake_program_address(vote_account_address, stake_pool, validator_seed_suffix) and find_transient_stake_program_address(vote_account_address, stake_pool, transient_seed_suffix), update_validator_list_balance must leave that entry completely unchanged, including last_update_epoch; otherwise an attacker-controlled stake account's lamports are recorded as pool assets, inflating total_lamports and the pool-token exchange rate.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_skips_pairs_with_wrong_pda

Balance_Updates.description: After update_validator_list_balance, the active_stake_lamports and transient_stake_lamports written into the entry at index start_index+i are read from the i-th supplied account pair and never exceed those two accounts' lamport balances, so a mis-pairing or over-count that would make the pool report stake it does not hold is impossible.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_records_balances_of_the_paired_accounts_only

Balance_Updates.description: update_validator_list_balance must record zero lamports for a validator or transient stake account whose Meta.authorized.staker/withdrawer is not the pool's withdraw-authority PDA or whose lockup differs from stake_pool.lockup (the Active branch currently records validator_stake_info.lamports() without that gate), otherwise total_lamports counts lamports the pool cannot move and the pool over-values itself.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_unusable_stake_not_counted

Balance_Updates.description: update_validator_list_balance may only advance an entry's status toward removal (DeactivatingAll -> DeactivatingTransient/DeactivatingValidator -> ReadyForRemoval); an entry that is Active before the call must still be Active after it, and no entry may move from ReadyForRemoval back to an active/deactivating status, otherwise a permissionless caller could eject a live validator (forcing its stake into the reserve) or resurrect an already-removed entry.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_status_only_moves_toward_removal

Balance_Updates.description: Any validator-list entry that update_validator_list_balance leaves with status ReadyForRemoval must have active_stake_lamports == 0 and transient_stake_lamports == 0, so that the later permissionless deletion of that entry by cleanup cannot change the pool's computed total_lamports.
Balance_Updates.title: ready_for_removal_entries_record_zero_lamports

Balance_Updates.description: update_validator_list_balance must leave the StakePool account's data byte-identical (it is a read-only input), so this signer-less instruction can never alter fees, authorities or recorded balances on the pool itself.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_does_not_modify_stake_pool_account

Balance_Updates.description: update_validator_list_balance must reject any account passed in the clock position whose key is not the Clock sysvar address; a forged clock lets entries be stamped with a far-future last_update_epoch while their balances stay stale, permanently defeating update_stake_pool_balance's staleness guard and freezing a wrong exchange rate into the pool.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_clock_must_be_canonical_sysvar

Balance_Updates.description: Both update_validator_list_balance and update_stake_pool_balance must reject any account passed as withdraw_authority other than create_program_address([stake_pool_address, "withdraw", stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed], program_id); an attacker-chosen authority would make stake_is_usable_by_pool accept foreign stake accounts as pool-controlled in the former, and would misdirect the fee-mint authority in the latter.
Balance_Updates.title: balance_updates_withdraw_authority_must_be_pool_pda

Balance_Updates.description: Both update_validator_list_balance and update_stake_pool_balance must reject a reserve_stake account whose key differs from stake_pool.reserve_stake and a validator_list whose key differs from stake_pool.validator_list, and must require both stake_pool and validator_list to be owned by this program; otherwise transient/validator stake is merged into an attacker-supplied stake account, or the pool's accounting is taken from a look-alike list.
Balance_Updates.title: balance_updates_reserve_and_list_pinned_to_stake_pool

Balance_Updates.description: When update_validator_list_balance is called with no_merge = true it must perform no stake-program merge CPI and must not change any entry's status, only refreshing recorded balances and last_update_epoch (today the Initialized validator-stake branch merges into the reserve and downgrades status regardless of the flag), otherwise the escape hatch intended for stake accounts in a bad state still aborts and the pool cannot be brought up to date.
Balance_Updates.title: no_merge_suppresses_all_merges

Balance_Updates.description: update_stake_pool_balance must fail if any validator-list entry has last_update_epoch strictly less than the current epoch, so that the pool's total_lamports can never be recomputed from per-validator balances that were not refreshed this epoch.
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_rejects_stale_validator_list

Balance_Updates.description: On success, update_stake_pool_balance sets stake_pool.total_lamports to exactly (reserve_stake.lamports - reserve Meta.rent_exempt_reserve - MINIMUM_RESERVE_LAMPORTS) plus the exact-integer sum over all validator-list entries of (active_stake_lamports + transient_stake_lamports), with no wrapping or truncation; any other value misprices every subsequent deposit and withdrawal. (Checked with the validator list bounded to a small number of entries, e.g. at most 4, for loop unrolling.)
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_total_lamports_exact

Balance_Updates.description: If the recomputed total lamports is not greater than stake_pool.total_lamports at entry, update_stake_pool_balance must mint zero pool tokens to the manager fee account, so that repeated permissionless calls in an epoch with no rewards cannot transfer value from stakers to the manager.
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_no_fee_without_rewards

Balance_Updates.description: The pool tokens minted as the manager's epoch fee by update_stake_pool_balance are worth at most epoch_fee.numerator/epoch_fee.denominator of the reward lamports, i.e. the lamports backing one pool token after the call is greater than or equal to its value before the call; a violation means fee minting dilutes existing holders beyond the advertised fee rate.
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_fee_does_not_dilute_holders

Balance_Updates.description: update_stake_pool_balance may change only total_lamports, pool_token_supply, last_update_epoch, last_epoch_total_lamports, last_epoch_pool_token_supply, epoch_fee, stake_withdrawal_fee, sol_withdrawal_fee and the three next_* staged-fee fields; manager, staker, validator_list, reserve_stake, pool_mint, manager_fee_account, token_program_id, stake_deposit_authority, sol deposit/withdraw authorities, deposit and referral fees, lockup, preferred validator addresses and stake_withdraw_bump_seed must be unchanged, and the validator list account data must be unchanged, since this signer-less handler rewrites the whole serialized struct.
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_preserves_pool_configuration

Balance_Updates.description: If stake_pool.last_update_epoch already equals the current epoch when update_stake_pool_balance is called, the call must leave epoch_fee, stake_withdrawal_fee, sol_withdrawal_fee, all three next_* staged-fee fields, last_epoch_total_lamports and last_epoch_pool_token_supply unchanged; otherwise repeated permissionless calls within one epoch fast-forward the FutureEpoch timelock and let the manager apply a raised withdrawal or epoch fee immediately.
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_fee_rollover_at_most_once_per_epoch

Balance_Updates.description: On an epoch-crossing update_stake_pool_balance, a staged fee held as FutureEpoch::Two(f) must become One(f) with the corresponding active fee unchanged, and only a field held as One(f) may write f into the active fee and then become None; a violation lets a manager-staged fee increase take effect earlier than the two-epoch delay stakers rely on.
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_staged_fee_advances_exactly_one_step

Balance_Updates.description: The only token CPI update_stake_pool_balance may perform is mint_to on stake_pool.pool_mint, targeting stake_pool.manager_fee_account, invoked on the program id stored in stake_pool.token_program_id and signed by the pool's withdraw-authority PDA; if any of those accounts is accepted unchecked, an attacker can have freshly minted pool tokens credited to an account they control or route the mint through a program they control.
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_mint_destination_pinned

Balance_Updates.description: With a validator list that is current for the epoch and an Initialized reserve stake account, update_stake_pool_balance must complete successfully even when the manager fee account fails check_manager_fee_info (wrong mint, uninitialized, frozen, unsupported extension), simply minting no fee; otherwise a broken manager fee account bricks epoch accounting and staged-fee rollover for the whole pool.
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_succeeds_with_invalid_fee_account

Balance_Updates.description: update_validator_list_balance must complete successfully, and stamp last_update_epoch = clock.epoch on every validator-list entry in [start_index, start_index + n), whenever it is given the pool's own validator_list and reserve_stake, a correctly derived withdraw_authority, the canonical Clock sysvar, an even number 2n of remaining accounts with start_index + n <= the validator list length, each pair equal to that entry's derived (validator, transient) stake PDAs, and a list whose entry status bytes are all valid StakeStatus values — and it must do so regardless of the on-chain state of the supplied stake accounts (uninitialized, non-stake data, activating, deactivating, an authority or lockup that does not match the pool); if any reachable stake-account state can make the whole chunk abort, the pool can never be refreshed, update_stake_pool_balance permanently fails its staleness check, and every deposit and withdrawal handler rejects with StakeListAndPoolOutOfDate, freezing user funds.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_well_formed_call_must_succeed

Balance_Updates.description: The only lamports update_validator_list_balance may move out of a validator stake account are those swept by a single stake-program withdraw whose amount is exactly validator_stake.lamports() minus stake.delegation.stake minus meta.rent_exempt_reserve, issued only when that quantity is strictly positive and the account's staker and withdrawer are the pool's withdraw-authority PDA and its lockup equals stake_pool.lockup, and whose destination is stake_pool.reserve_stake; sweeping more would break the validator stake account's rent exemption or remove delegated pool stake, and sweeping less (or computing the excess without subtracting the rent-exempt reserve) leaves lamports stranded outside the pool's recorded accounting.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_excess_lamport_sweep_amount_exact

Balance_Updates.description: The pool tokens minted to the manager fee account by update_stake_pool_balance must be computed from the epoch_fee value stored in the stake pool at the start of the call, before any FutureEpoch rollover copies next_epoch_fee into epoch_fee — so that when the call crosses an epoch boundary with next_epoch_fee == One(f) and f differs from epoch_fee, the minted amount equals the fee computed with the old epoch_fee; otherwise a manager-staged fee increase is applied retroactively to rewards that accrued while the lower fee was in force, defeating the notice period the FutureEpoch timelock gives stakers.
Balance_Updates.title: uspb_fee_uses_epoch_fee_active_at_entry

Balance_Updates.description: For every validator-list entry that update_validator_list_balance refreshes, every lamport held at the start of the call by that entry's validator stake account and transient stake account that is usable by the pool (Meta.authorized.staker == Meta.authorized.withdrawer == the pool's withdraw-authority PDA and Meta.lockup == stake_pool.lockup) must, when the call returns, either be recorded in that entry's active_stake_lamports/transient_stake_lamports or have been moved out of those accounts by one of the call's CPIs into the reserve stake account (or into the entry's own validator stake account, whose resulting balance is what active_stake_lamports records); the concrete gap is the validator-stake Stake(meta, stake, _) arm for an entry whose status is DeactivatingValidator or DeactivatingAll with no_merge == false, where a stake account that is usable by the pool but still merely deactivating (deactivation_epoch == clock.epoch, i.e. for the whole epoch in which RemoveValidatorFromPool ran) takes neither the no_merge branch nor the inactive-merge branch and is therefore recorded as 0 while still holding the full delegated stake plus rent, so that any user can permissionlessly call this handler and then update_stake_pool_balance to make the pool's total_lamports understate its assets by a removed validator's entire stake, minting pool tokens too cheaply and redeeming withdrawals too poorly for the rest of the epoch, and turning the next epoch's recovery into a phantom reward on which the manager collects the epoch fee.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_records_all_pool_usable_lamports

Balance_Updates.description: Every stake-program merge CPI that update_validator_list_balance issues must be given a source and destination that are mergeable at clock.epoch: when the destination is the reserve stake account the source must be fully inactive (Initialized, or a Stake whose delegation.deactivation_epoch < clock.epoch, or whose activation_epoch == deactivation_epoch == clock.epoch), and when the destination is the entry's validator stake account both source and destination must be fully active (delegation.activation_epoch < clock.epoch AND delegation.deactivation_epoch == u64::MAX) — the merge-into-validator-stake arm currently tests only activation_epoch < clock.epoch on both sides, so a transient stake deactivated earlier in the same epoch by DecreaseValidatorStake or RemoveValidatorFromPool qualifies while the stake program classifies it MergeTransientStake and rejects the CPI, aborting the whole chunk so that none of its entries can be stamped for the epoch, which in turn makes update_stake_pool_balance fail its staleness check and every deposit, withdrawal and rebalancing instruction revert with StakeListAndPoolOutOfDate until the next epoch boundary.
Balance_Updates.title: uvlb_merge_only_between_mergeable_states

SOL_Deposits.description: If stake_pool.sol_deposit_authority is Some(a) before the call, deposit_sol and deposit_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the optional trailing sol_deposit_authority account is actually supplied, its key equals a, and it is a signer; otherwise anyone could deposit into a permissioned (private) pool and mint its pool tokens against the operator's policy.
SOL_Deposits.title: private_pool_requires_sol_deposit_authority_signature

SOL_Deposits.description: deposit_sol and deposit_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the reserve_stake account passed in has the key stored in stake_pool.reserve_stake, since otherwise the depositor's lamports are transferred to an attacker-chosen destination while stake_pool.total_lamports is still credited and pool tokens are still minted, leaving the pool insolvent.
SOL_Deposits.title: reserve_stake_account_must_equal_pool_reserve_stake

SOL_Deposits.description: deposit_sol and deposit_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the stake_pool account is owned by this program and has account_type == StakePool, pool_mint equals stake_pool.pool_mint, manager_fee_account equals stake_pool.manager_fee_account, token_program equals stake_pool.token_program_id, and system_program is the canonical System Program id; otherwise an attacker can redirect the mint or the fee tokens, or route the lamport transfer through a program they control.
SOL_Deposits.title: deposit_sol_account_binding_to_pool_state

SOL_Deposits.description: deposit_sol and deposit_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the withdraw_authority account equals create_program_address([stake_pool.key, "withdraw", stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed], program_id), and every mint_to CPI they issue must be invoke_signed with exactly those seeds and that authority, so that a substituted account can never cause the program to sign a token mint with an attacker-influenced PDA.
SOL_Deposits.title: mint_authority_pda_rederived_from_stored_bump

SOL_Deposits.description: On a successful deposit_sol or deposit_sol_with_slippage, stake_pool.total_lamports after equals stake_pool.total_lamports before plus lamports_in exactly (no wrapping or saturation), and the single System Program transfer CPI moves exactly lamports_in from lamports_from to stake_pool.reserve_stake; any divergence makes the recorded pool value inconsistent with the reserve's real balance and mis-prices every later deposit and withdrawal.
SOL_Deposits.title: total_lamports_increases_by_exactly_deposited_amount

SOL_Deposits.description: On a successful deposit_sol or deposit_sol_with_slippage, the increase in stake_pool.pool_token_supply equals exactly the sum of the amounts passed to the mint_to CPIs for the user token account, the manager fee account and the referrer account (all on stake_pool.pool_mint); if the recorded supply and the amount actually minted diverge, the exchange rate is corrupted for every holder.
SOL_Deposits.title: pool_token_supply_increase_equals_total_minted

SOL_Deposits.description: For a successful deposit_sol or deposit_sol_with_slippage on a pool whose pool_token_supply was strictly positive before the call, total_lamports_after * pool_token_supply_before >= total_lamports_before * pool_token_supply_after over exact integers, i.e. the depositor never receives more than their pro-rata share and cannot extract value from existing holders.
SOL_Deposits.title: sol_deposit_does_not_dilute_existing_holders

SOL_Deposits.description: Every successful deposit_sol or deposit_sol_with_slippage mints a strictly positive number of pool tokens to dest_user_pool_token_account, so a deposit whose post-fee token amount rounds to zero must be rejected rather than silently taking the caller's lamports for nothing.
SOL_Deposits.title: sol_deposit_mints_nonzero_tokens_to_user

SOL_Deposits.description: deposit_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the number of pool tokens minted to the user is greater than or equal to minimum_pool_tokens_out, since otherwise the caller's slippage guard is decorative and a rate change between submission and execution silently gives them fewer tokens than they demanded.
SOL_Deposits.title: sol_deposit_slippage_bound_enforced

SOL_Deposits.description: deposit_sol and deposit_sol_with_slippage must fail whenever stake_pool.last_update_epoch is less than the current epoch, because minting against a total_lamports figure that predates this epoch's rewards and epoch fee prices the deposit at a stale exchange rate and lets the depositor extract value from existing holders.
SOL_Deposits.title: sol_deposit_rejected_when_pool_is_stale

SOL_Deposits.description: On a successful deposit_sol or deposit_sol_with_slippage, the tokens minted to the manager fee account plus those minted to the referrer equal exactly ceil(new_pool_tokens * sol_deposit_fee.numerator / sol_deposit_fee.denominator) (zero when the denominator is zero), the referrer's portion equals floor(that fee * sol_referral_fee / 100), and the user receives exactly the remainder; since the referrer account is entirely caller-chosen and unvalidated, this is what bounds how much an arbitrary referrer can be minted.
SOL_Deposits.title: sol_deposit_fee_split_is_exact

SOL_Deposits.description: A successful deposit_sol or deposit_sol_with_slippage leaves every StakePool field other than total_lamports and pool_token_supply unchanged — in particular manager, staker, validator_list, reserve_stake, pool_mint, token_program_id, stake_withdraw_bump_seed, stake_deposit_authority, sol_deposit_authority, sol_withdraw_authority, last_update_epoch and all fee fields — because the handler re-serializes the whole struct and an offset or deserialization bug there would silently rewrite pool configuration or authorities.
SOL_Deposits.title: sol_deposit_only_modifies_supply_and_total_lamports

SOL_Deposits.description: For a program-owned, valid, up-to-date pool with sol_deposit_authority set to None, correctly bound reserve/mint/fee/token-program accounts and a lamports_in large enough that the post-fee token amount is nonzero, deposit_sol must succeed and mint tokens, ensuring the guards are not collectively so strict that the permissionless deposit flow is dead.
SOL_Deposits.title: permissionless_sol_deposit_is_reachable

SOL_Deposits.description: A deposit_sol of L lamports immediately followed by a withdraw_sol burning exactly the pool tokens just received, in the same epoch and with no intervening state change, must return at most L lamports; this property spans a two-instruction sequence (and reaches into the SOL Withdrawals handler), so it is more expensive to check than the single-handler properties, but a violation is a risk-free drain of the reserve driven by rounding direction.
SOL_Deposits.title: sol_deposit_then_withdraw_round_trip_not_profitable

SOL_Deposits.description: On a successful deposit_sol or deposit_sol_with_slippage, the increase in stake_pool.pool_token_supply equals exactly lamports_in when total_lamports before the call was 0 or pool_token_supply before the call was 0, and otherwise equals exactly floor(lamports_in * pool_token_supply_before / total_lamports_before) over exact integers with no truncating cast; any other value means the deposit is priced off the pool's real exchange rate, over-minting steals from every existing holder and under-minting silently confiscates part of the depositor's lamports.
SOL_Deposits.title: exact_pool_token_amount_matches_exchange_rate

SOL_Deposits.description: Starting from identical pool state and identical accounts, deposit_sol(lamports_in) and deposit_sol_with_slippage(lamports_in, minimum_pool_tokens_out = 0) must succeed under exactly the same conditions and produce identical results — the same increase in stake_pool.total_lamports, the same increase in stake_pool.pool_token_supply, the same lamports amount in the System transfer CPI and the same three mint_to amounts — since the two entry points differ only by a slippage guard; this is a relational property requiring two runs from a shared symbolic start state, and a violation means the slippage entry point deposits or mints an amount unrelated to what the caller requested (e.g. the two u64 payload fields being forwarded positionally in the wrong order).
SOL_Deposits.title: slippage_variant_matches_base_variant_at_zero_minimum

SOL_Deposits.description: For a program-owned, valid, up-to-date stake_pool whose sol_deposit_authority is Some(a), with correctly bound reserve_stake, pool_mint, manager_fee_account, token_program and system_program accounts, a trailing eleventh account whose key equals a and which is a signer, and a lamports_in large enough that the post-fee user token amount is nonzero, deposit_sol must succeed and mint tokens to the user, so that the permissioned-deposit branch of the authority check and the optional-trailing-account plumbing are not collectively so strict that a private pool is dead and no funds — not even the configured authority's — can ever enter it.
SOL_Deposits.title: private_pool_sol_deposit_is_reachable

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake (DepositStake and DepositStakeWithSlippage) must abort unless the stake_pool account is owned by the stake-pool program and has account_type StakePool, and the validator_list account is owned by the stake-pool program, has header account_type ValidatorList, and its key equals stake_pool.validator_list; otherwise an attacker can supply a look-alike pool or a fabricated validator list containing a forged Active entry and have the pool's accounting written into an account they control.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_state_accounts_program_owned_and_bound

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake must abort unless the withdraw_authority account equals Pubkey::create_program_address([stake_pool.key, "withdraw", stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed], program_id), because that account is used as the signing authority for the pool-token mint_to, the stake merge, and the excess-lamport stake withdraw; accepting any other key would let the pool's PDA signature be applied on behalf of an unrelated authority.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_withdraw_authority_must_be_pool_pda

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake must abort unless the stake_deposit_authority account key equals stake_pool.stake_deposit_authority, and, when that key differs from find_deposit_authority_program_address(program_id, stake_pool), unless that account is a signer of the transaction; otherwise a pool configured as private (custom stake deposit authority) can be deposited into by anyone, defeating the pool's deposit gate.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_deposit_authority_matches_and_signs_when_custom

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake must abort unless pool_mint == stake_pool.pool_mint, manager_fee_account == stake_pool.manager_fee_account, token_program == stake_pool.token_program_id, and stake_program == the native stake program id; otherwise deposit fee tokens can be redirected to an attacker's account, or the mint_to/stake CPIs can be pointed at an attacker-controlled program while the pool withdraw-authority PDA supplies the signature.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_infrastructure_accounts_pinned_to_pool_record

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake must abort unless the reserve_stake account key equals stake_pool.reserve_stake, because the handler withdraws the deposit's excess (non-delegated) lamports out of the validator stake account into that account using the pool withdraw-authority PDA as signer; an unchecked destination lets an attacker have pool lamports paid to an account they own.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_reserve_must_equal_pool_reserve

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake must abort unless the validator_stake_account key equals find_stake_program_address(program_id, validator_stake.delegation.voter_pubkey, stake_pool.key, NonZeroU32::new(entry.validator_seed_suffix)) for the matched validator-list entry, so that user stake can only ever be merged into a stake account that this program controls for this pool; without the re-derivation an attacker could have the deposit merged into a stake account they control while still receiving pool tokens.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_target_must_be_derived_validator_stake_pda

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake must abort unless the validator list contains an entry whose vote_account_address equals the target validator stake account's delegation.voter_pubkey and whose status is exactly StakeStatus::Active; depositing into a validator marked DeactivatingValidator/DeactivatingTransient/DeactivatingAll/ReadyForRemoval mints pool tokens against stake that is being removed from the pool's accounting.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_validator_entry_must_exist_and_be_active

Stake_Deposits.description: When stake_pool.preferred_deposit_validator_vote_address is Some(v), process_deposit_stake must abort unless the target validator stake account's delegation.voter_pubkey equals v; otherwise the staker's routing constraint (which exists to stop users using the pool as a free conversion between validators) can be bypassed.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_respects_preferred_deposit_validator

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake must abort when stake_pool.last_update_epoch < clock.epoch, so that pool tokens are never minted at an exchange rate computed from total_lamports/pool_token_supply that predates the current epoch's reward accrual; minting at a stale ratio lets a depositor capture unbooked rewards from existing holders.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_requires_pool_updated_this_epoch

Stake_Deposits.description: For process_deposit_stake, with T/S the pool's total_lamports/pool_token_supply before and T'/S' after, T' * S >= T * S' must hold (exact integer arithmetic), i.e. the lamport value backing each pool token never decreases as a result of a deposit; a violation means an attacker can mint pool tokens worth more than the stake they deposited, stealing value from existing holders.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_does_not_dilute_existing_holders

Stake_Deposits.description: On a successful process_deposit_stake, stake_pool.total_lamports increases by exactly d — the increase in the validator stake account's lamports caused by the merge — and stake_pool.pool_token_supply increases by exactly floor(d * S / T) (or by d when T == 0 or S == 0), computed over exact integers with no wraparound; any other update desynchronizes the pool's recorded backing from the lamports it actually received.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_supply_and_total_lamports_updated_exactly

Stake_Deposits.description: On a successful process_deposit_stake, the tokens credited to the user, to stake_pool.manager_fee_account, and to the referrer must sum exactly to the increase in stake_pool.pool_token_supply, with total_fee = ceil(tokens_from_stake * stake_deposit_fee.numerator / denominator) + ceil(tokens_from_sol * sol_deposit_fee.numerator / denominator), referral = floor(total_fee * stake_referral_fee / 100), manager = total_fee - referral, and user = minted_total - total_fee; a mismatch either over-charges the depositor or mints tokens that are unaccounted for in the fee split.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_fee_split_is_exact_and_matches_configured_rates

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake must abort with DepositTooSmall rather than succeed when the pool tokens credited to the depositor round to zero, so that a deposit can never transfer lamports into the pool while minting nothing to the depositor (a silent donation that inflates every other holder's claim).
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_user_tokens_nonzero

Stake_Deposits.description: DepositStakeWithSlippage must abort with ExceededSlippage unless the pool tokens credited to the depositor *after* stake/SOL deposit fees and referral share are deducted are at least minimum_pool_tokens_out, and with minimum_pool_tokens_out = 0 it must behave exactly as DepositStake; checking the gross pre-fee amount instead would let the pool honour a deposit that delivers the user less than they demanded.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_with_slippage_enforces_minimum_on_net_user_tokens

Stake_Deposits.description: In process_deposit_stake, the amount withdrawn from the validator stake account to the reserve must be at most d (the lamport increase produced by merging the user's stake), and the reserve stake account's lamports must never decrease across the handler; otherwise a deposit could siphon lamports that were already delegated to the validator out of the validator stake account.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_excess_withdraw_bounded_by_this_deposit

Stake_Deposits.description: A successful process_deposit_stake must change exactly one ValidatorStakeInfo entry — the one whose vote_account_address matches the target validator's vote account — and only its active_stake_lamports field, leaving the list length, header (account_type, max_validators), and every other entry's fields byte-identical; a BigVec index/offset error that touched a neighbouring entry would silently corrupt another validator's recorded stake.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_modifies_only_the_matched_validator_entry

Stake_Deposits.description: After a successful process_deposit_stake, the matched entry's active_stake_lamports must equal the validator stake account's actual lamport balance at the end of the instruction (i.e. after the merge and after the excess lamports were withdrawn to the reserve); drift here mis-prices later withdrawals and rebalances.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_entry_lamports_match_validator_stake_account

Stake_Deposits.description: A successful process_deposit_stake must leave every StakePool field other than total_lamports and pool_token_supply unchanged — in particular manager, staker, stake_deposit_authority, sol_deposit/withdraw authorities, validator_list, reserve_stake, pool_mint, token_program_id, all fee fields, both bump seeds, last_update_epoch and the preferred validator addresses — so that a deposit can never be used to reconfigure or take over the pool.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_leaves_pool_configuration_unchanged

Stake_Deposits.description: If the user-supplied stake_account is the same account as the pool's reserve stake account or as the target validator_stake_account (no distinctness check is made in the handler), a caller could have the pool 'deposit' lamports it already owns and mint itself pool tokens for them; process_deposit_stake should reject when the source stake account aliases any pool-owned stake account passed in the same instruction.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_source_must_not_alias_pool_owned_stake_accounts

Stake_Deposits.description: The handler never inspects the deposited stake account's own delegation, relying entirely on the native stake program's merge to reject a mismatch; if a stake account delegated to a different vote account (or in a non-Stake state, or with a different lockup/authorities) could be merged, the pool would credit one validator's entry with stake delegated elsewhere, so process_deposit_stake should reject unless the source stake account's delegation.voter_pubkey equals the target validator's vote account.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_source_delegation_must_match_target_validator

Stake_Deposits.description: A well-formed deposit — pool up to date for the current epoch, program-derived (permissionless) stake deposit authority, an Active validator-list entry matching the correctly derived validator stake PDA, no preferred deposit validator or a matching one, correct mint/fee/reserve/token-program accounts, and an amount large enough to round to nonzero user tokens — must succeed and mint a nonzero number of pool tokens to the depositor; if no such input exists, the deposit path is dead and the pool cannot accept stake.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_legitimate_deposit_is_reachable

Stake_Deposits.description: On a successful process_deposit_stake (DepositStake and DepositStakeWithSlippage), the pool tokens credited to the depositor must be worth no more than the lamports the deposit actually delivered to the pool: over exact integers, pool_tokens_user * stake_pool.total_lamports_after <= total_deposit_lamports * stake_pool.pool_token_supply_after; a violation means the depositor mints a claim on lamports that were already in the pool and did not come from their deposit.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_depositor_claim_never_exceeds_deposited_lamports

Stake_Deposits.description: On a successful process_deposit_stake, the pool tokens minted to the referrer must equal floor(stake_deposit_fee_tokens * stake_pool.stake_referral_fee / 100) + floor(sol_deposit_fee_tokens * stake_pool.sol_referral_fee / 100) with the manager fee account receiving the rest of the total fee, so that the referral share of the excess-lamport ("SOL") portion of a stake deposit is governed by sol_referral_fee exactly as it is in DepositSol; applying the stake referral rate to the SOL-fee portion misdirects fee tokens between the depositor-chosen referrer and the manager.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_referral_split_uses_the_matching_referral_rate_per_fee_category

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake parses a StakeStateV2 out of validator_stake_account without ever verifying that account is owned by the native stake program, yet it derives from that parsed data the vote account address used to select the validator-list entry and to test the preferred-deposit-validator constraint, the stake-vs-SOL split that decides which deposit-fee rate applies, and the number of lamports withdrawn out of that account to the reserve under the withdraw-authority PDA signature; the handler should reject unless validator_stake_account.owner equals the native stake program id, since today the sole defense against a fabricated stake account is the PDA address re-derivation.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_validator_stake_account_owner_not_checked

Stake_Deposits.description: For a pool whose stake_deposit_authority differs from find_deposit_authority_program_address(program_id, stake_pool), a well-formed deposit in which that exact authority account is a signer must succeed and mint a nonzero number of pool tokens to the depositor; if no such input exists the private-pool branch of the deposit-authority dispatch (plain invoke of stake authorize rather than invoke_signed) is dead and every private pool is permanently unable to accept stake deposits.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_private_pool_deposit_is_reachable_with_signing_custom_authority

Stake_Deposits.description: On a successful process_deposit_stake (DepositStake and DepositStakeWithSlippage), with T = stake_pool.total_lamports and S = stake_pool.pool_token_supply read before the handler and d = the lamport increase the merge produced in the validator stake account, the total pool tokens minted (user + manager fee + referral, i.e. the increase in stake_pool.pool_token_supply) must be at least floor(d * S / T) when T > 0 and S > 0 — equivalently, over exact integers, minted * T + T > d * S — and the handler must abort rather than fall back to a 1:1 rate when exactly one of T and S is zero; otherwise the depositor is silently short-changed, and in the reachable T == 0 / S > 0 state (a pool drained of lamports while dust pool tokens remain outstanding, since calc_lamports_withdraw_amount yields 0 for them and they can never be burned) every new deposit is minted 1:1 and immediately shared with that stranded supply.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_prices_deposit_at_no_worse_than_current_rate

Stake_Deposits.description: process_deposit_stake never reads the source stake account's data, so it cannot tell a user's stake account from stake the pool already owns and has already counted in stake_pool.total_lamports; the handler should reject when the source stake account's Meta.authorized.withdrawer, before the instruction runs, equals the pool's withdraw-authority PDA (the authority on every validator, transient and ephemeral stake account of this pool, none of which are passed as accounts here so no key-equality check can catch them), because merging such an account into the target validator stake account would make the handler measure the resulting lamport movement as a fresh deposit, add it to total_lamports a second time, and mint pool tokens to the caller for stake the pool already held — today the sole barrier is the native stake program refusing the authorize CPI, i.e. a check that lives entirely in the callee.
Stake_Deposits.title: deposit_stake_source_must_not_already_be_pool_owned_stake

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake and withdraw_stake_with_slippage must fail unless the passed token_program account key equals stake_pool.token_program_id and the passed pool_mint key equals stake_pool.pool_mint; otherwise an attacker supplies a look-alike token program (which is used verbatim as the CPI program id for burn/transfer_checked) or a foreign mint, so the pool-token burn is a no-op while the stake split still executes, yielding free stake.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_token_program_and_mint_pinned_to_pool

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake and withdraw_stake_with_slippage must fail unless the passed manager_fee_account key equals stake_pool.manager_fee_account, so the withdrawal fee cannot be redirected to an attacker-chosen token account.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_manager_fee_account_pinned

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake must fail unless the stake_pool account is owned by this program with account_type == StakePool, and the validator_list account is owned by this program, has header account_type == ValidatorList, and its key equals stake_pool.validator_list; substituting an attacker-controlled validator list would let the caller fake 'no validator has active or transient stake' and take the withdrawal straight out of the reserve or drain a validator entry.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_pool_and_validator_list_authenticity

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake must fail unless the passed withdraw_authority account key equals the address derived from seeds [stake_pool, "withdraw", stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed] under this program id, since that PDA signs the stake split and the authorize CPIs that hand the new stake account to the user.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_withdraw_authority_is_canonical_pda

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake must fail when stake_pool.last_update_epoch is less than the current epoch read from the canonical Clock sysvar, so that pool tokens can never be redeemed against a stale total_lamports/pool_token_supply exchange rate that predates this epoch's reward accrual or fee collection.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_rejects_stale_pool

Stake_Withdrawals.description: If stake_split_from is stake_pool.reserve_stake, withdraw_stake must fail whenever any entry of the validator list has active_stake_lamports or transient_stake_lamports greater than the required minimum plus one lamports-per-pool-token tolerance, so that users cannot bypass the validator-stake withdrawal priority and drain the reserve while delegated stake is still available (bound the validator list to a small number of entries, e.g. 2-3, for checking).
Stake_Withdrawals.title: reserve_withdrawal_only_when_all_validators_drained

Stake_Withdrawals.description: On success of withdraw_stake, the source account must belong to the highest non-empty priority tier: if some validator entry has active_stake_lamports above the minimum-plus-tolerance threshold then stake_split_from must equal the canonical validator stake PDA derived from the source's delegated vote account, the pool, and that entry's validator_seed_suffix; if no entry has such active stake but some entry has transient stake above the threshold then stake_split_from must equal the transient stake PDA derived with that entry's transient_seed_suffix; violating this lets a user pick a favourable source and skew the pool's delegation.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_source_tier_priority_respected

Stake_Withdrawals.description: If stake_pool.preferred_withdraw_validator_vote_address is set and the corresponding validator list entry's active_stake_lamports exceeds the required minimum plus tolerance, withdraw_stake must fail unless the stake account being split is delegated to that preferred vote account; otherwise the staker's routing constraint (which exists to stop users using the pool as a free conversion between validators) can be bypassed.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: preferred_withdraw_validator_enforced

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake must fail if the validator list entry matching the source stake account's delegated vote account has a status other than Active (DeactivatingTransient, DeactivatingValidator, DeactivatingAll or ReadyForRemoval), so that stake already scheduled for removal cannot be withdrawn out from under the pool's removal bookkeeping.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_only_from_active_status_validator_entry

Stake_Withdrawals.description: For withdraw_stake and withdraw_stake_with_slippage, the pool's exchange rate must not decrease for the remaining holders: total_lamports_after * pool_token_supply_before >= total_lamports_before * pool_token_supply_after (exact integer arithmetic), which is equivalent to the withdrawer receiving no more than their pro-rata share floor(burnt_tokens * total_lamports / pool_token_supply); a violation is direct value extraction from the other pool-token holders.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_never_decreases_lamports_per_pool_token

Stake_Withdrawals.description: On success of withdraw_stake, stake_pool.pool_token_supply must decrease by exactly (pool_tokens - withdrawal_fee_tokens) — the fee tokens are transferred to the manager, not burnt, so they must remain counted in supply — and stake_pool.total_lamports must decrease by exactly the number of lamports actually split out of the source account; any mismatch permanently corrupts the pool's redemption rate.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_exact_supply_and_lamports_bookkeeping

Stake_Withdrawals.description: On success of withdraw_stake with a validator or transient stake source, the decrease of that entry's active_stake_lamports (Active and ValidatorRemoval sources) or transient_stake_lamports (Transient source) must equal the decrease of stake_pool.total_lamports; when the source is the reserve, no validator list entry may change at all, so per-validator accounting never drifts from the pool total.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: validator_entry_decrement_equals_total_lamports_decrement

Stake_Withdrawals.description: On success of withdraw_stake, the pool tokens taken as fee must be exactly ceil(pool_tokens * stake_pool.stake_withdrawal_fee.numerator / denominator) — rounded up, never down — and must not exceed pool_tokens, except in the two documented exemptions (the burn source is the manager fee account, or the manager fee account fails its token-account validity check) where the fee must be exactly zero; a wrong rounding direction or an unclamped fee silently leaks manager revenue or over-charges users.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: stake_withdrawal_fee_is_exact_ceiling_of_configured_rate

Stake_Withdrawals.description: On success of withdraw_stake from an active or transient validator stake account, the lamports remaining in the source (its pre-call balance minus the lamports split out) must be at least meta.rent_exempt_reserve + max(stake program minimum delegation, MINIMUM_ACTIVE_STAKE); otherwise the pool is left with an under-funded or non-rent-exempt stake account it can no longer merge or manage.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: source_stake_account_keeps_minimum_remaining_lamports

Stake_Withdrawals.description: On success of withdraw_stake with stake_split_from == stake_pool.reserve_stake, the reserve's pre-call lamports minus the lamports split out must still be at least minimum_reserve_lamports (its rent-exempt reserve); the handler currently only checks that the reserve's balance *before* the withdrawal covers the minimum and delegates the post-condition to the native stake program's split validation, so if that delegation is ever wrong the reserve can be pushed below rent exemption.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: reserve_withdrawal_must_check_post_withdrawal_balance

Stake_Withdrawals.description: On success of withdraw_stake_with_slippage, the number of lamports actually split out must be at least minimum_lamports_out; the slippage comparison is performed on the pre-truncation amount while the full-validator-removal branch afterwards truncates withdraw_lamports down to the source account's balance, so a user can receive up to lamports_per_pool_token fewer lamports than the minimum they demanded.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: slippage_bound_applies_to_final_withdrawn_lamports

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake must fail rather than succeed with zero lamports split out, so a user can never burn pool tokens (and pay a withdrawal fee) while receiving nothing.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_never_burns_tokens_for_zero_lamports

Stake_Withdrawals.description: On success of withdraw_stake, the validator list's element count and every entry other than the one matching the source stake account's delegated vote account must be byte-identical to before; within the modified entry, vote_account_address, validator_seed_suffix, transient_seed_suffix and last_update_epoch must be unchanged, and only the relevant lamports field and (in the removal case) status may change — this catches index/offset errors in the BigVec find_mut path (check with the list bounded to 2-3 entries).
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_modifies_only_the_matching_validator_entry

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake may set a validator list entry's status to ReadyForRemoval only if that entry's active_stake_lamports ends at exactly zero; marking an entry ready for removal while it still accounts for active lamports strands those lamports when CleanupRemovedValidatorEntries deletes the entry.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: ready_for_removal_only_when_entry_fully_drained

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake must not set a validator list entry's status to ReadyForRemoval while that entry's transient_stake_lamports is nonzero; the handler's precondition is the pool-wide 'no transient stake above required_lamports + lamports_per_pool_token' test, which tolerates a nonzero transient balance, so a user can fully drain a validator stake account and have the entry (and later, at cleanup, the row) removed while a transient stake account delegated under it is still live and unaccounted for.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: ready_for_removal_requires_zero_transient_stake

Stake_Withdrawals.description: If withdraw_stake marks the validator list entry of stake_pool.preferred_withdraw_validator_vote_address (or preferred_deposit_validator_vote_address) as ReadyForRemoval, it must also clear that preference, as RemoveValidatorFromPool does; otherwise once CleanupRemovedValidatorEntries deletes the row, every subsequent withdraw_stake fails with ValidatorNotFound at the preferred-validator lookup, freezing all stake withdrawals until the staker intervenes.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: preferred_withdraw_validator_never_left_dangling

Stake_Withdrawals.description: On success of withdraw_stake, all StakePool fields other than total_lamports, pool_token_supply (and, per the preferred-validator property, the preferred validator addresses) must be unchanged — manager, staker, validator_list, reserve_stake, pool_mint, manager_fee_account, token_program_id, both bump seeds, lockup, all fee fields and last_update_epoch — so that a withdrawal cannot be used to silently re-point or re-configure the pool via a mis-sized serialization.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_leaves_pool_configuration_unchanged

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake must reject a stake_split_to account that equals stake_split_from, equals stake_pool.reserve_stake, or equals any validator/transient stake PDA of this pool, because the handler afterwards uses the withdraw-authority PDA to authorize stake_split_to's staker and withdrawer to a user-chosen key; today this is prevented only by the native stake program refusing to split into an initialized account, which the verifier models as an unconstrained callee (check with the validator list bounded to 2-3 entries).
Stake_Withdrawals.title: split_destination_must_not_be_a_pool_owned_stake_account

Stake_Withdrawals.description: A user holding sufficient pool tokens must be able to complete withdraw_stake against an up-to-date pool that has one Active validator entry whose stake account holds well above the minimum, with all correctly derived accounts and user_transfer_authority signing — i.e. the priority, minimum-remaining-stake and fee guards must not be collectively so strict that no withdrawal path exists.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: legitimate_withdrawal_is_reachable

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake must still be able to source from stake_pool.reserve_stake when every validator-list entry whose active_stake_lamports or transient_stake_lamports exceeds the required-minimum-plus-tolerance threshold has a status other than Active — i.e. the pool-wide `has_active_stake` / `has_transient_stake` availability tests must range only over entries that are legally usable as a withdrawal source (status == Active), because an entry marked DeactivatingValidator/DeactivatingAll/DeactivatingTransient/ReadyForRemoval keeps its full active_stake_lamports until a later balance update, yet is rejected as a source by the status check, so counting it makes the handler refuse the reserve ('validator stake accounts have lamports available') while simultaneously refusing the only account that has the lamports, freezing all stake withdrawals for up to an epoch even though the reserve is fully funded (check with the validator list bounded to 2 entries).
Stake_Withdrawals.title: reserve_withdrawal_reachable_when_only_ineligible_validators_hold_stake

Stake_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_stake and withdraw_stake_with_slippage must fail unless the stake_split_from account is owned by the native stake program, because the handler deserializes that account's raw data with try_from_slice_unchecked::<StakeStateV2> and then trusts two values from it — meta.rent_exempt_reserve, which becomes required_lamports / minimum_lamports_with_tolerance (the pool-wide threshold that selects the Active/Transient/ValidatorRemoval/reserve tier, the minimum-remaining-stake guard, and minimum_reserve_lamports in the reserve branch) and delegation.voter_pubkey, which selects the ValidatorList entry that gets decremented — so a look-alike, non-stake-program account whose bytes merely parse as a stake state lets the caller set the pool's own withdrawal-priority threshold and choose which validator row is debited.
Stake_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_stake_source_must_be_owned_by_native_stake_program

Stake_Withdrawals.description: If stake_pool.preferred_withdraw_validator_vote_address is set, no validator-list entry has active_stake_lamports above required_lamports plus the one-pool-token tolerance (so the withdrawal falls into the transient tier), and the preferred validator's entry has transient_stake_lamports above that same threshold, then withdraw_stake must fail unless the stake account being split is delegated to the preferred vote account; the handler's preferred-validator gate compares only against the preferred entry's active_stake_lamports and is therefore vacuous in the transient tier, letting a user route the withdrawal to any other validator's transient stake account and use the pool as the free conversion between validators that SetPreferredValidator exists to prevent (check with the validator list bounded to 2-3 entries).
Stake_Withdrawals.title: preferred_withdraw_validator_unenforced_for_transient_tier

SOL_Withdrawals.description: If stake_pool.sol_withdraw_authority is Some(k), then withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the optional trailing account is supplied, its key equals k, and it is a signer; otherwise anyone could drain a private pool's reserve without the configured gatekeeper's consent.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: private_pool_requires_sol_withdraw_authority_signature

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the passed reserve_stake account key equals stake_pool.reserve_stake, so that an attacker cannot substitute another stake account controlled by the same withdraw-authority PDA (e.g. a validator or transient stake account) and have lamports withdrawn from it.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: reserve_stake_account_pinned_to_pool_state

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the withdraw_authority account equals the program address derived from [stake_pool_key, "withdraw", stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed] under this program id, with the bump taken from pool state rather than instruction data, so that no attacker-supplied account can stand in as the pool's stake-withdraw signer.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: withdraw_authority_must_be_canonical_pool_pda

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the stake_pool account is owned by this program and its deserialized account_type is StakePool; otherwise a look-alike account could supply attacker-chosen reserve_stake, pool_mint, manager_fee_account and withdraw-bump fields and redirect the withdrawal.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: stake_pool_account_owned_by_program_and_initialized

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when stake_pool.last_update_epoch is greater than or equal to the current Clock epoch, so that pool tokens are never redeemed at a stale exchange rate that has not yet absorbed the epoch's rewards or fees.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: stale_pool_rejects_sol_withdrawal

SOL_Withdrawals.description: On a successful withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage, stake_pool.pool_token_supply decreases by exactly the number of tokens burned (pool_tokens minus the withdrawal fee tokens, which are transferred rather than burned) and stake_pool.total_lamports decreases by exactly the lamport amount withdrawn from the reserve; any other decrease or increase corrupts the pool's accounting of assets versus shares.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: supply_and_total_lamports_decrease_exactly

SOL_Withdrawals.description: The lamports withdrawn equal floor(pool_tokens_burnt * stake_pool.total_lamports_before / stake_pool.pool_token_supply_before) (and zero when the pre-state supply is zero), so that withdrawn_lamports * supply_before <= burnt * total_lamports_before and the withdrawal can never pay out more than the burned shares' pro-rata claim nor reduce the lamports-per-pool-token of the remaining holders.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: sol_withdraw_amount_is_pro_rata_floor_no_over_withdrawal

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the reserve stake account deserializes to StakeStateV2::Initialized(meta) and its lamports minus the withdrawn amount is at least meta.rent_exempt_reserve + MINIMUM_RESERVE_LAMPORTS (which also implies the withdrawal never exceeds the reserve's balance); otherwise the reserve could be pushed below rent exemption and be reaped, or the CPI could be attempted for more lamports than exist.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: reserve_remains_initialized_and_rent_exempt_after_withdrawal

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage must fail (WithdrawalTooSmall) whenever the computed lamport payout rounds to zero, so a user's pool tokens are never burned and fee tokens never taken in exchange for no SOL.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: zero_lamport_sol_withdrawal_rejected

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol_with_slippage may only succeed when the computed lamports out is at least minimum_lamports_out, and withdraw_sol behaves exactly as withdraw_sol_with_slippage would with minimum_lamports_out = 0; otherwise the caller's slippage protection against an adverse exchange rate is silently ineffective.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: slippage_minimum_lamports_out_enforced

SOL_Withdrawals.description: On a successful SOL withdrawal, the tokens leaving the user's burn_from account are exactly pool_tokens = tokens_burned + fee_tokens_transferred_to_manager, where fee_tokens equals ceil(pool_tokens * stake_pool.sol_withdrawal_fee.numerator / denominator) and is zero when the fee denominator is zero, when the burn source is the manager fee account, or when the pinned manager fee account fails validation; a fee exceeding pool_tokens or an inexact split would over-charge the user or silently under-collect the pool's fee.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: user_pool_tokens_conserved_and_fee_computed_exactly

SOL_Withdrawals.description: A successful withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage leaves every other StakePool field unchanged — account_type, manager, staker, stake_deposit_authority, bump seeds, validator_list, reserve_stake, pool_mint, token_program_id, last_update_epoch, all fee and next-fee fields, preferred validators and the funding authorities — so that a mis-serialization on the withdrawal path cannot silently reconfigure the pool.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: sol_withdrawal_mutates_only_supply_and_total_lamports

SOL_Withdrawals.description: The token burn and fee-transfer CPIs issued by withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage must target the program in stake_pool.token_program_id, act on the mint stake_pool.pool_mint, send fee tokens only to stake_pool.manager_fee_account, and the lamport-moving stake withdrawal must be signed only with the [stake_pool_key, "withdraw", stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed] seeds; anything else lets a caller redirect the pool's PDA authority or its fee stream.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: sol_withdrawal_cpis_pinned_to_pool_configured_targets

SOL_Withdrawals.description: For an up-to-date pool with no configured sol_withdraw_authority, a correctly derived withdraw authority, a reserve holding well above its rent-exempt minimum, and a user burning a modest amount of pool tokens, withdraw_sol must be able to succeed — the accumulated guards must not make the SOL withdrawal path unreachable and strand user funds.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: legitimate_sol_withdrawal_is_reachable

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage must only succeed when the account it names as the token-burn/fee-transfer authority (the `user_transfer_authority` account, index 2) has is_signer == true; the pool program itself never checks this flag and relies entirely on the SPL Token CPI to reject an unsigned authority, so if that delegation is ever unsound anyone could destroy a third party's pool tokens and drain the corresponding lamports out of the reserve to an address of their choosing.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: token_burn_authority_must_be_a_signer

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage must only succeed when the reserve_stake account passed in is owned by the native stake program, because the handler deserializes that account's raw data as StakeStateV2 and uses meta.rent_exempt_reserve as the sole bound on how much SOL may leave the reserve; check_reserve_stake compares only the pubkey, so if the pool's reserve_stake ever points at an account owned by another program the attacker chooses the rent-exempt floor and the SolWithdrawalTooLarge guard becomes vacuous.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: reserve_rent_floor_derived_from_stake_program_owned_account
