SOL_Withdrawals.description: For an otherwise valid, up-to-date pool with sufficient reserve, withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage must still be able to succeed — charging zero fee and performing no fee transfer — when the pinned stake_pool.manager_fee_account is uninitialized, not owned by stake_pool.token_program_id, holds a different mint, or carries an unsupported token extension; otherwise the manager could permanently freeze every user's SOL withdrawal simply by breaking their own fee-receiving token account.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: broken_manager_fee_account_must_not_block_sol_withdrawals

SOL_Withdrawals.description: withdraw_sol / withdraw_sol_with_slippage must only succeed when the `burn_from_pool_token_account` it is given (account index 3) is owned by `stake_pool.token_program_id` — the same account it also uses as the source of the fee transfer — because the handler reads no field of that account before decrementing `stake_pool.pool_token_supply` by `pool_tokens_burnt` and releasing `withdraw_lamports` from the reserve; if that delegated check is ever unsound, an attacker supplies a look-alike account under a program they control, no pool tokens leave circulation, and the reserve is drained while the pool's share accounting is silently written down.
SOL_Withdrawals.title: pool_token_supply_decrement_requires_genuine_pool_token_burn_source

Token_Metadata.description: Neither CreateTokenMetadata nor UpdateTokenMetadata may succeed unless the account passed in the `manager` position is a transaction signer and its key equals the `manager` field of the supplied `stake_pool` account; otherwise any caller could rewrite the pool token's on-chain name/symbol/uri and deface or impersonate the pool token.
Token_Metadata.title: metadata_only_pool_manager_may_create_or_update

Token_Metadata.description: CreateTokenMetadata and UpdateTokenMetadata must both fail unless the `metadata_account` key equals the Metaplex-derived PDA for `stake_pool.pool_mint` (seeds "metadata", mpl program id, mint), and CreateTokenMetadata must additionally fail unless `pool_mint` equals `stake_pool.pool_mint`; otherwise the pool's withdraw-authority PDA signature is aimed at the metadata of a mint unrelated to the pool (confused deputy).
Token_Metadata.title: metadata_account_bound_to_pool_mint

Token_Metadata.description: CreateTokenMetadata must fail unless the `payer` account is a signer and is owned by the System program; if the owner check were absent a caller could name a program-owned account (the stake pool account itself, a reserve/validator stake account) as payer and have its lamports consumed to fund the metadata account's rent.
Token_Metadata.title: create_metadata_payer_must_sign_and_be_system_owned

Token_Metadata.description: The only program that CreateTokenMetadata and UpdateTokenMetadata invoke under the withdraw-authority PDA's signature is the hard-coded Metaplex token-metadata program id (and, in create, the hard-coded System program id); if the callee id were read from an unvalidated account, an attacker could redirect a PDA-signed CPI to arbitrary code acting as the pool's withdraw authority.
Token_Metadata.title: metadata_cpi_target_is_pinned_program_id

Token_Metadata.description: In both CreateTokenMetadata and UpdateTokenMetadata, the `withdraw_authority` account that was validated against the pool (create_program_address over [stake_pool, "withdraw"] with `stake_pool.stake_withdraw_bump_seed`) must be exactly the address produced by the signer seeds passed to invoke_signed (which use the canonical bump from find_withdraw_authority_program_address), so the program never validates one authority and signs as another; note these two handlers are the only ones in the program that sign with the canonical bump instead of the pool's stored bump.
Token_Metadata.title: metadata_signing_seeds_match_validated_withdraw_authority

Token_Metadata.description: After CreateTokenMetadata or UpdateTokenMetadata returns successfully, every field of the `stake_pool` account (account_type, manager, staker, pool_mint, reserve_stake, validator_list, all fee fields, total_lamports, pool_token_supply, bump seeds) is identical to its pre-state and the handler itself moves no lamports between the passed accounts; the metadata path must not be a route to editing pool accounting or authorities.
Token_Metadata.title: metadata_handlers_leave_stake_pool_state_unchanged

Token_Metadata.description: CreateTokenMetadata and UpdateTokenMetadata must fail unless the `stake_pool` account is owned by the stake-pool program and its deserialized `account_type` is `StakePool`; otherwise a caller can supply a system-created, program-owned account containing an arbitrary byte blob and have `manager`, `pool_mint` and the withdraw bump read from data they chose.
Token_Metadata.title: metadata_requires_initialized_program_owned_stake_pool

Token_Metadata.description: With an initialized, program-owned stake pool, the real manager signing, the pool's canonical withdraw-authority PDA, the pool's own mint, a system-owned signing payer, the correctly derived Metaplex metadata PDA and the pinned Metaplex/System program ids, CreateTokenMetadata and UpdateTokenMetadata must reach the Metaplex CPI rather than erroring out — i.e. the guards are not so strict that the manager can never publish pool token metadata.
Token_Metadata.title: metadata_manager_flow_is_reachable
